* Launch polish: surface engagement features + Discord /drops

Site: a 'Save more & win big' section on the homepage with cards linking to
Forge Coins, Mystery boxes and the Drop calendar — so the new features are
actually discoverable (bilingual).

Discord: new /drops command showing the upcoming drop calendar (live from the
store, with Discord relative timestamps) + a link to the full calendar;
registered and added to /help.

* Live trust stats: refresh instantly on delivery + new review (no fabrication)

The trust stats (delivered count, customers, review count, average rating) are
already computed 100% from real DB rows — nothing seeded or padded (demoSeed
only inserts products; no hardcoded numbers in the UI). This makes them update
INSTANTLY instead of within the 15s cache window: bust the social/stats cache
the moment an order is marked delivered and the moment a review is added, so
the counters and average rating move up right away.

Verified on real Postgres: delivered increments on completion, review count +
rating reflect a real review; boots with no circular-import issue.

* Launch-ready hardening: zero-admin setup, critical fixes, self-running maintenance

Critical fixes:
- productSchema rejected kind='mystery' (enum was digital|physical) → the
  admin's Mystery box toggle could never save. Added 'mystery'.
- Admin fulfillment badge counted status='paid', which doesn't exist →
  always 0. Now counts payment_received/processing/awaiting_fulfillment.

Zero-admin launch:
- Self-scheduling maintenance: piggybacks on live traffic (max 1×/hour per
  instance, non-blocking) so OTP purges, stale-order cleanup and payment
  reminders run WITHOUT CRON_SECRET or Vercel Cron. Launch-check item is
  now ok by default (cron stays as optional backup).
- Starter content on first boot (idempotent, never overwrites admin work):
  the €49.99 Forge Mystery Box with a balanced 5-prize pool (EV ≈ €38.75 →
  ~22% margin, paid as store credit) + an FPS Duo bundle (Apex+Valorant,
  10% off). 'mystery' category gets its own card visual.

Quality:
- Mystery-only orders now AUTO-COMPLETE on payment (the credit payout IS
  the delivery) instead of lingering in the manual queue.
- Forge Shop: redeemed coupon codes persist in the coin history with a
  copy button (a toast was the only place you ever saw the code).

Verified on real Postgres: 5/5 hardening e2e (maintenance fires on traffic,
launch-check ok without CRON_SECRET, mystery auto-complete, fulfillment
query, code-in-history) + 4/4 starter-content e2e + 19/19 regression suite;
build green.

* Discord relay: full automation with ZERO hosting-side Discord secrets + badge fix

The 'Discord automation' launch warning could only be cleared by putting the
bot token / webhook URLs into Vercel. Now the community bot (which already has
the token) pulls the store's events itself:

- Migration 017: discord_outbox queue + a tiny kv table.
- discordService: every sender (order pings, drops, stock alerts, 500 alerts)
  posts directly when a webhook is configured, and otherwise QUEUES the exact
  embed payload in the outbox. Delivery DMs relay the same way (channel 'dm'
  with the buyer's linked Discord id) when no server-side bot token exists.
- POST /api/discord/outbox — HMAC-signed like the digest; returns + marks
  pending events, stamps 'bot seen' in kv, prunes old rows.
- Bot: polls the outbox every 60s and posts events to #leads / #deals (with
  fallbacks) or DMs the buyer. Zero new env vars — reuses REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET.
- Launch check: 'Discord automation' turns OK as soon as the bot has polled in
  the last 24h ('Bot connected via relay'), with a clear hint otherwise.

Also: the admin Support badge now counts only OPEN tickets (action needed), so
resolving a ticket clears the badge — 'pending' means waiting on the customer.

Verified on real Postgres over real HTTP: queue → signed poll → delivered →
second poll empty → bad signature 403 → launch check flips to ok (8/8);
bot load test + build green.

* bot: watchdog retries before paging (cold start / Neon wake is not an outage)

The site watchdog alerted @here after a single failed 15s probe — but a
serverless cold start plus a sleeping Neon database can take 15-25s to wake,
which is a false alarm, not downtime. Verified the API itself is healthy: a
cold boot from a COMPLETELY fresh database (all 17 migrations + seeds) answers
/api/health in ~1.3s, warm in ~12ms. Now the watchdog retries once after 20s
with a 28s timeout and only pages when both probes fail — real outages still
alert within ~1 minute.

* Fix everything reported live + product art + email v3

Fixes from live testing:
- Duplicate €49.99 mystery boxes: the starter seeder raced when Vercel booted
  several instances at once. Now uses a FIXED primary key (insert ON CONFLICT
  DO NOTHING) and heals existing duplicates on boot (keeps the oldest; deletes
  or deactivates extras). Verified with 3 parallel seed calls → exactly 1 box.
- 'Fortnite Accounts' removed from the home sidebar — it was a hardcoded entry
  pointing at the v-bucks category; we don't sell accounts.
- 'Happy customers' now counts people who actually WROTE A REVIEW (stat tile +
  hero avatar row), not everyone who ever ordered — and hides at zero.
- Orders badge vs Fulfillment badge: Orders now shows paid orders awaiting
  delivery; Fulfillment counts exactly the manual queue its page displays.
- Forge Coins grant bug: the order-earn dedupe index blocked a second grant by
  the same admin (same reason+ref) — grants now store ref NULL (attribution is
  in the audit log).

New:
- Write a review on /reviews: verified buyers pick one of their delivered
  orders (new GET /account/reviewable), star + text → posts via the existing
  verified-review endpoint. Guests see how reviews work. Bilingual.
- Admin → Users: 🪙 Coins button to give (or deduct) Forge Coins per user
  (POST /admin/security/users/:id/coins, audited, can't go below 0).
- Product art: per-pack denomination cards (the existing pack SVGs) now win
  over the generic category icon, and syncCatalogImages() backfills them on
  every boot so the LIVE catalog gets its art too.
- Email v3: richer shell for ALL mails (patterned gradient header, badge,
  pill styles) + a redesigned login-code email (lock badge, expiry pill).
  Previous body registered as legacy so deployed DBs auto-upgrade.

Proven on real Postgres (8/8): parallel-seed dedupe, duplicate healing, double
grant, over-deduct block, redeemed code REALLY gives €10 off €25 at checkout,
single-use enforced, reviewable query, queue count. Build green.

* starter: heal duplicate bundles (6x FPS Duo Pack from the pre-fix race)

The old bundle seeder created a random-id bundle per concurrent cold start
before the fixed-id fix shipped, leaving 6 identical 'FPS Duo Pack' rows in
production. Boot now dedupes same-named bundles (keeps the oldest, tiebreak
on id for same-instant rows; bundles have no dependents so DELETE is safe).

Reproduced exactly (6 identical rows, 3 sharing one timestamp) → heals to 1;
parallel re-runs stay at 1 (3/3 on real Postgres).

* Audit round: reroll safety, phone-route crash fix, /balance Discord command

- rerollPull: validate the pull + a non-empty reward pool BEFORE atomically
  claiming the one-time reroll, so an emptied pool can no longer burn the
  buyer's free reroll and crash the request.
- account routes: import badRequest (phone verify routes threw a 500
  ReferenceError on any invalid input instead of a clean 400).
- New signed endpoint POST /api/discord/balance: Forge Coins, store credit
  and loyalty tier for a linked Discord member; the uid is bound into the
  HMAC signature so requests can't be replayed for another member.
- Bot: new /balance command (ephemeral) + /help entry; unlinked members get
  a login pointer.

Verified on real Postgres: 23-check purchase-flow e2e (createOrder ->
payment -> mystery settle -> coins -> auto-complete -> reroll paths),
7-check balance-endpoint HTTP e2e, 19-check regression suite, bot load
test, vite build.

* Add /clearpins staff command to bulk-delete "pinned a message" notices

Every time something is pinned, Discord posts a small "X pinned a message to
this channel" system message. Our setup panels pin on boot, so these pile up.

/clearpins (staff-only) walks the history of every text + announcement channel
and deletes just those pin-notice system messages (MessageType 6) in one go —
normal messages and other system notices are left untouched. Deletes
individually so notices older than 14 days are handled too, paginating up to a
safety cap per channel. Optional `here:true` limits it to the current channel.
Reports how many were removed and calls out any channels it lacked
Manage Messages / Read Message History for.

Verified with a mocked-interaction test: only pin notices deleted across text +
announcement channels, voice channels not scanned, unmanageable channels
skipped and reported; bot load test + lint still green.

* Document REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET in the bot .env.example

The bot needs REVIEW_INGEST_SECRET to poll the signed store relay (order
pings, drops, delivery DMs) and to read /balance and /digest, but it was
missing from the example env file — easy to forget when deploying to a host.
Add it with a note that it must match the value in Vercel, and point the
store URLs at the live domain.

* Fix 5 bugs found in a full site + Discord audit

Frontend
- Checkout page crashed on render: the main component called t() dozens of
  times but never ran useI18n() (only the helper sub-components did), so the
  whole checkout threw a ReferenceError the moment the cart had items. Nobody
  could reach the pay step. Added const { t } = useI18n().

Server
- Gift-card codes were derived purely from Date.now() mod 32, so only 32
  distinct codes could ever be generated — trivially guessable/enumerable
  (drain any outstanding card via the public balance check + redeem) and
  colliding on the UNIQUE index after a few issues. Now generated with
  crypto.randomInt over a 32-char alphabet (~10^24 space); proven 20000/20000
  unique.
- Manual-payment proof confirm/reject never notified the buyer: it checked
  order.user_id, but getOrder() hydrates to camelCase order.userId, so the
  guard was always false. Fixed both call sites; the reject email's order link
  was also an empty string — now points at the public track page.

Discord bot
- Auto-moderation + XP ran inside CLAIMED tickets: claiming renames the
  channel to '✋-ticket-…', which defeated the startsWith('ticket-') check, so
  a customer pasting a trade link in their own claimed ticket got their
  message deleted and publicly warned. Detect tickets by their stable
  'ticket-owner:' topic (survives the rename) via a shared isTicketChannel().
- /suggest could report 'interaction failed' while actually posting: it did
  two Discord round-trips (send + startThread) before its first reply, risking
  the 3s ACK window. Now defers first, then edits the reply.

Verified on real Postgres + mocked-bot: new bugfix e2e (7 checks: proof
confirm/reject notifications, gift-card uniqueness/shape), ticket-exemption
test (scam in a claimed ticket is left alone, public channel still moderated),
gift-card entropy (20000/20000 unique), plus the full suite green — flow-e2e
(23), regression (19), bot load test, and vite build.

* Auto-email gift-card codes to the recipient on issue

Issuing a gift card with a recipient email now delivers the code straight to
that inbox with a new branded 'gift_card' template (code, amount, note, and a
redeem-in-your-wallet call to action) — previously the recipient email was
stored but nothing was ever sent, so staff had to copy the code and send it by
hand. Best-effort: a mail failure never invalidates the (already valid) card;
the API + admin UI report whether it was emailed. Leaving the email blank still
just generates a code to hand out yourself.

The new template auto-rolls out to the live DB via syncEmailTemplates on boot.

Verified on real Postgres: issuing with a recipient logs a gift_card email
whose subject carries the amount and whose rendered code matches the card;
issuing without one sends nothing and the card is still valid (8 checks).

* Add automatic post-delivery review-request email

Every completed order now gets one 'How was your order?' email a day after
delivery, linking straight to the review widget for that order on /track
(works for guest buyers too). Idempotent and self-scheduling: it runs from the
existing maintenance pass (no cron needed), stamps review_request_sent_at
before sending so it never repeats, and skips any order that already has a
review. New migration 018 adds the column + a partial index; the new
review_request template auto-installs on the live DB via syncEmailTemplates.

This completes the customer email journey: order received -> payment
confirmed -> completed (with the delivered code) -> review request.

Verified on real Postgres (8 checks): sent once 24h+ after completion, not for

* Fix slow first request (cold start): defer non-critical boot work

Symptom: signup / 'send code' could take ~15s. Cause: ensureReady() — which the
serverless handler awaits before EVERY request on a cold instance — ran heavy
upkeep synchronously on each boot: ~11 email-template queries, per-product art
backfill across the whole catalog (~70+ products), and starter-content dedupe.
On a cold Neon connection those ~100 sequential round-trips stacked up before
the request (and its OTP email) even started.

Now ensureReady only awaits what a request truly needs — migrate (schema),
seed on an empty DB, and stocking an empty catalog — and defers the rest
(syncEmailTemplates upgrade, seedStarterContent, syncCatalogImages) to a
one-shot background task that runs after we're ready to serve.

Measured locally: on an already-seeded DB the blocking boot dropped from doing
~100 queries to 3 (~36ms); on cold Neon that removes the multi-second stall.
The empty-DB path is unchanged (seed() still installs roles/permissions/all
templates synchronously, so auth + OTP work on the very first request).

Verified: boot e2e (6 checks — roles, catalog and login_otp template ready
immediately; 2nd ensureReady memoised; starter box + bundle appear via
background upkeep). Regression (19), lint, build green.

- Serial queue (fulfillmentService): on payment, instead of firing a per-order
  fulfillment, we drain a queue that processes paid supplier orders ONE AT A
  TIME, oldest first — finishing (buy + deliver) one before starting the next.
  A short DB lease (kv row + TTL) guarantees only one worker drains at a time
  across serverless instances; an 'attempted' set advances past orders that open
  no request (margin-guarded) instead of looping; async in-progress buys are
  re-polled from maintenance. Also drained from maintenance as a safety net.

* Audit round: fix payment, coin, and supplier auto-buy money/security bugs

Full audit of the manual-payments, supplier auto-buy, Forge+/coins/wallet,
trust-stats, cold-start and security surfaces. Stats, cold-start, DB
parameterization, admin authz and secret handling verified solid; the
confirmed defects below are fixed and covered by e2e tests.

Payments
- orderService: make the order status transition atomic (conditional UPDATE
  guarded on the observed status + change check). Concurrent confirms / a
  webhook racing a manual confirm can no longer dispense, email or complete an
  order twice.
- paymentProofService: atomically claim a proof (UPDATE ... WHERE status=
  'pending') so a double-click / second admin can't drive a second
  markPaymentReceived; reject non-http(s) screenshot links (zod .url() also
  passes javascript:/data:, a stored-XSS vector in the admin queue); flag the
  2nd proof as multiple_submissions (was off-by-one at the 3rd).
- catalog: reject the screenshot URL at the route too; disable the demo
  self-pay route whenever a real payment method is configured.
- Checkout: show the server order total on the pay-instructions screen — the
  cart is cleared first, so the old cart-derived amount read €0.00.

Forge Coins / membership
- forgeCoinService: lock the user row (FOR UPDATE) before summing in
  spendCoins/redeemReward/grantCoins, matching walletService. Concurrent
  spends can no longer both pass the balance check (negative balance / free
  rewards / free membership).
- account: charge + grant membership in one transaction (no "charged without
  membership", no partial grant).

Supplier auto-buy
- Kinguin/Eldorado: never mark an order fulfilled with zero delivered keys —
  a transient error fetching the keys kept the order in_progress to re-poll
  instead of completing it empty-handed (paid supplier, buyer got nothing).
- fulfillment margin guard: treat an unknown (null) supplier cost as
  do-not-auto-buy, and compare cost to the buyer's effective post-discount
  revenue per unit instead of list price (no blind uncapped buys, no buying at
  a loss on discounted orders).
- G2A: fix the doubled /v3 path prefix (every call 404'd), pass order
  quantity with a line-level max_price cap, and collect multiple keys.

- Home header: gap-6 across all items burned ~96px of width on phones,

  Sign Up (arrow hidden on xs). Page fits 390px exactly.
- Checkout steps: four full labels + connectors overflowed 390px; on phones
  only the active step keeps its label. Shop, product, pay, track, cart and
  rewards verified clean.

Tests in-repo + CI
- server/test/: the ten e2e suites (audit fixes, semiauto fulfillment,
  margin queue, discord invite, regression, supplier autofulfill, supplier
  queue, kinguin/g2a/guard connectors) with relative imports, plus
  run-all.mjs which runs each suite against its own freshly-created Postgres
  database so suites can never pollute each other. `npm test` in server/.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: on every PR/push — frontend build, Discord-bot
  syntax check, and the full suite against a real Postgres 16 service.

Verified: npm test → all 10 suites green locally; proof alert lands in
discord_outbox with order number + admin link; mobile re-sweep shows
scrollWidth == clientWidth on both fixed pages; npm run build green.

* Delivery choice (gift code vs account top-up) + email order summary + price-bug fix

Delivery choice
- Products can offer the buyer a choice at checkout: a gift code (emailed) or a
  direct top-up to their account (like a Roblox top-up). Product form gets a
  "let the buyer choose" toggle next to the delivery-target label; when off but
  a target is set, the account target stays mandatory (pure top-up product).
- Checkout shows the choice only when a cart item offers it; picking "account"
  reveals the required target field. The pick is stored as billing.deliveryMethod
  ('code' | 'account'); a supplied target implies account delivery (backward
  compatible with the pre-choice checkout).
- Account top-ups are ALWAYS hand-delivered — autoDispenseFromStock skips them so
  a stock code is never leaked for a direct top-up. They surface in the manual
  queue with an "account top-up" badge + the username; the fulfill modal drops
  the code field (owner just confirms).

Emails
- The order summary now renders a real breakdown (subtotal, each discount, store
  credit, bold total) — fixes the mismatch where a line item showed the list
  price (€9.99) but the total showed the discounted amount (€4.49) with no
  explanation.
- The completion email hero is method-aware: a premium copyable code card for
  code orders, or a green "delivered straight to your account" confirmation
  (with the username, no code) for top-ups. All inline-styled so it survives
  clients that strip <style>.
- New renderOrderEmail() helper renders an order email to {subject, html} for
  previews and tests.

Verified: new delivery-choice suite 17/17 (account skips auto-dispense, lands in
the queue, completes on confirm, email shows the account confirmation without
leaking a code; code order auto-dispenses + emails the code; summary breakdown
reconciles), full server suite green, npm run build green, emails rendered to
PNG and checked for both delivery methods.

* Premium order_completed email (Clean Premium Receipt), auto-upgrade on deploy

Redesigns the order-complete email into a premium, fully inline-styled layout
(status pills, "Your loot is ready" hero, the delivery hero, a labelled Order
summary breakdown, gradient CTA, support line) — inline styles survive clients
that strip <style>. Direction chosen via a design panel (3 directions judged).

The previous default body is added to LEGACY_TEMPLATE_BODIES so syncEmailTemplates
upgrades existing installs whose stored template is still the old default (an
admin-customized template is left untouched).

* Set the permanent Discord invite (discord.gg/CrAfqENsSV) as the fallback

Replaces the old invite everywhere it's hardcoded as a fallback — env config,
the bot's /invite fallback, and the storefront community + drops pages. The
live bot still keeps a never-expiring invite in sync on top of this once it runs.

* Replace Orbitron headings with Space Grotesk (cleaner, premium)

Community feedback: the display font read as "ugly". Swaps the loud sci-fi
Orbitron heading font for Space Grotesk — modern, premium, still with a tech/
gaming character and much more legible. Keeps Inter for body and Rajdhani for
small uppercase labels. The legacy `font-orbitron` Tailwind token is aliased to
the new display font so no element ever requests an unloaded typeface.
Chosen by rendering candidates (Orbitron vs Space Grotesk vs Sora) side by side.

* Mystery box: hide the odds — keep it a mystery

Removes the visible win-percentages on the mystery-box product page (the prize
list stays, so buyers still see what they can win). The weights/odds are no
longer sent to the client at all, so the chances can't be read from devtools
either — the mystery stays a mystery. Admin still manages weights as before.

* Fix: custom product Image URL no longer reset to the default icon

The catalog art sync ran on every boot and forced each demo product's image
back to its shipped 3D icon — so an Image URL set in Admin → Products saved,
then got overwritten on the next deploy/cold start. Both the boot-time
syncCatalogImages and the demo-seed backfill now only set the default cover
when the product has NO image; an owner-set image is always preserved. Clearing
the Image URL field falls back to the default icon again (a natural reset).

* Admin products: search + bulk-set one image across a selection

Adds a search box to the products list (matches name / category / SKU) and a
"select all matches" shortcut — so you can type "robux", grab every variant,
and apply ONE image URL to the whole selection in a single click. Select-all
now operates on the filtered matches.

The bulk endpoint gains an `image` action: sets (or clears, with an empty
value) metadata.image across every selected product; only real http(s) URLs are
accepted. Combined with the earlier fix, an owner-set image now sticks.

* Premium logo plinth behind product images (uniform for any logo)

Adds a reusable .fm-logo-plinth tray + .fm-logo treatment: a soft rounded
background with a subtle violet glow disc and an inner ring, and a drop shadow
on the image. Mixed product logos — transparent PNGs or badge-style marks —
now read as one cohesive, premium set. Applied to the home Popular Products
tiles and the storefront product cards (LightProductCard).

* Headings: Space Grotesk → Bricolage Grotesque (more character, premium)

Final type polish. Bricolage Grotesque gives the headings a warmer, more
"designed" editorial feel than the plainer Space Grotesk, while staying modern
and highly legible. Body stays Inter, small labels stay Rajdhani; the legacy
display token aliases follow. Chosen by rendering candidates (Space Grotesk vs
Bricolage vs Outfit vs Sora) with the real fonts and the actual hero text.

* Hero glow-up: coloured halos behind each floating logo + livelier float

Gives each hero logo a soft brand-tinted glow halo (the signature look of the
target mockup) and a livelier, varied up-and-down float with gentle rotation
(three staggered variants + a breathing halo). Bigger logos, fuller arrangement,
stronger podium glow. The logos already load from the icon PNGs, so once real
brand PNGs are dropped in they appear here automatically — floating, haloed.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion. Build green; rendered on desktop + mobile.

* Fallback to category logo when a product image fails to load

A missing or 404'ing product image showed the browser's ugly broken-image
placeholder over the gradient. Product detail hero and storefront cards now
detect the load error (onError) and render the category logo centred on the
gradient instead.

* Product images: Pinterest links + gallery upload; smarter search

Images:
- Owner can upload a product image straight from their device/gallery. The
  file is downscaled + inlined as a data URI (no blob store needed), on both
  the product editor and the bulk 'one image for the whole selection' toolbar.
- Pasting a page link (e.g. a Pinterest pin) now resolves to the real image
  behind it via a new admin resolve-image endpoint (og:image / twitter:image),
  with an SSRF guard blocking internal hosts.
- Image values are validated centrally (isSafeImageValue): site paths, http(s)
  links and raster data URIs are allowed; javascript:/svg/html URIs rejected.

Search:
- Storefront (command palette + shop filter) and the admin product search now
  ignore case, spaces and punctuation, so 'vbucks' matches 'V-Bucks'.

Tests: new imageUrl unit suite (safe-value, SSRF guard, og:image, resolver
via mock fetch) + a data-URI acceptance case in the bulk-image suite.

* Fit owner-supplied product images cleanly into card & hero

An uploaded/linked image with its own (often white) background showed as a
hard box floating on the tile. Custom images (isCustomImage: not /products/*)
now render as a contained logo over a soft blurred backdrop of themselves, so
the background blends edge-to-edge instead of clipping or floating. Built-in
pack/category logos keep their plinth treatment.

Note: on the card the artwork is force-positioned relative by .fm-card-media,
and a % max-height there resolves against the auto grid track (ignored), so the
size cap uses fixed px.

* Fix: uploaded product images larger than 1mb now save

Uploading a real photo/logo silently failed to save — the base64 image
exceeded Express' 1mb JSON body limit, so the request 413'd and the product
never changed. Raised the body limit to 3mb (still guarded by isSafeImageValue,
now capped at 2.5mb) and made the client encoder compress uploads: photos are
re-encoded as JPEG with a size budget (PNG kept only when the image truly has
transparency), so a phone-sized image lands well under the limit.

Adds a large-image regression test (1.4mb saves, oversized → 400, bulk too).

* Admin list shows the saved product image; point OG/sitemap at forgemarket.nl

Two things made saving an image feel broken even though it saved:
- The admin Products list rows always rendered a fixed category icon, never
  product.image — so after a successful save the thumbnail looked identical.
  Rows now show the actual image when one is set (desktop + mobile).
- index.html OG tags and robots.txt hardcoded the legacy forgemarket-store.
  vercel.app domain instead of the canonical forgemarket.nl, which invites
  viewing/sharing a different deployment than the admin. Repointed to
  forgemarket.nl.

Also give the ⌘K command-palette product cache a 60s TTL so catalog edits
show without a full reload.

* Remove flat image backgrounds; show product artwork in the category hero

- New removeSolidBackground(): edge flood-fill makes a uniform (e.g. white)
  background transparent with a feathered fringe, so an uploaded logo/render
  blends onto the card instead of sitting in a white box. Non-uniform images
  (real photos/banners) are detected and left untouched.
- Uploads now auto-strip a flat background, and the product editor gets a
  'Remove background' button to clean images uploaded earlier (works on the
  data-URI already on the product).
- The shop category banner now shows the owner's own product artwork instead
  of the generic category icon.

* Per-category logos, managed in the admin

The owner can now give every category its own logo instead of the built-in
icons, and the storefront renders them everywhere categories appear.

- New Admin -> Categories page lists every category being sold, each with its
  current art, an upload button and a paste-a-link field. Uploads auto-strip a
  flat background, a page link (e.g. a Pinterest pin) resolves to its image,
  and each logo can be background-stripped or reset to the default.
- Logos persist as a {slug: image} map in the kv table via a small
  settingsService, exposed to the storefront on the public /api/config the SPA
  already fetches, and read through a shared, de-duplicated useCategoryLogos
  hook.
- Rendered on the home category list + popular tiles, the shop sidebar and the
  category banner, each falling back to the built-in icon when unset.
- Image values reuse the product-image guard, so only site paths, http(s)
  links and raster data URIs are accepted.

Adds a category-logos regression suite (set/read/clear, unsafe value rejected,
staff-only).

* Replace the flat category icons with a real 3D icon set

The old icons were flat shapes floating on a big coloured blob, half a
megabyte each. They now come from a generator (scripts/gen-icons.mjs) that
draws every icon from shared primitives, so the whole set reads as one family:
a single light from the top-left, an extruded side face for real depth, a
glossy specular highlight and a soft contact shadow.

- Archetypes cover the catalogue: stacked hex/round coins for game currency,
  faceted crystals for gems, glossy app tiles, spheres, a controller, chest,
  gift card, banknote, shopping bag and a voxel cube.
- SVG instead of PNG: the whole set is 180 KB (was 16 MB) and stays crisp at
  any size. Icon ids are namespaced per file — duplicate gradient/clip ids
  cross-wire when several icons share a document.
- Products already storing the old .png icon path are repointed to .svg on
  boot, so nothing renders broken. Owner uploads and links are untouched.

Also fixes the shop hero art: .fm-hero-brand > * forced position:relative,
which overrode the art's absolute placement and dropped it on top of the
heading. It now opts out via .fm-hero-art and sits on the right, and the
'All Products' banner shows real art instead of an outline emoji.

* Use the owner's own brand artwork for the main categories

Ten logos were uploaded to public/products/icons. Each needed different
treatment, so scripts/prep-brand-icons.mjs records the recipe per file and
turns them into tidy 256px square icons:

- Logos on a flat background (Robux, V-Bucks, Valorant, Nitro, Steam, gift
  card) get the background knocked out and a feathered edge, then trimmed and
  centred, so they sit on the tile without a white box.
- Solid-colour marks where the colour IS the design (PlayStation, Xbox, Call
  of Duty) keep their background and get rounded corners like an app tile.
- The EA FC source was a promo banner, so it's cropped to the FC Points pile
  — which also drops the headline text and the other shop's watermark.

Icon paths now resolve the extension per category (iconPath): these ten are
raster, the rest keep the generated 3D SVGs. Products stored against the other
extension are repointed on boot, in both directions, so switching a category
between its own art and the generated icon never leaves a broken image.

* Hero: stop the feature cards covering the artwork, and give type real roles

The four feature cards were absolutely positioned over the top-right of the
hero, which is exactly where the floating logos sit — PlayStation, Nitro and
Xbox were buried underneath them. The cards now take their own grid column
once there is room for one, and the page gets a wider cap on large monitors
(it was leaving ~500px unused at 1920) so the headline stops wrapping and the
buttons stay on one row.

Typography: .fm-head was used in ten places — the brand mark, prices, stat
figures — but was never defined in any stylesheet, so all of it silently fell
back to body Inter. Defining it, plus a .fm-num role, gives four families with
one job each: Bricolage Grotesque for display, Inter for reading, Space
Grotesk for numbers (tabular, so prices line up), Rajdhani for small caps.

Verified across 1280/1440/1920: no logo/card overlap, headline on one line,
and the type roles resolve to the intended families.

* Group every gift card under one category

Store credit sat in eight categories with a single product each (Steam,
PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Amazon, Google Play, iTunes, Netflix), which made
the catalogue and the category list look scattered. All ten now share the
'giftcard' category.

Each product keeps its own brand art, so grouping them doesn't flatten the
lot to one generic gift-card icon: the seed pins an image per product, and the
storefront's fallback catalogue does the same via a per-SKU brand map.
Subscriptions (Spotify, Game Pass, Discord Nitro) stay where they are — a
3-month plan isn't a gift card.

Existing products are moved by SKU on boot, so a live database regroups itself
instead of needing the categories changed by hand.

Verified against a database seeded the old way: 8 categories → giftcard=10,
every product still on its own logo, the Gift Cards page lists all ten with no
broken images.

* Launch audit batch 1: stop the storefront undermining its own credibility

Every fix here removes something that actively cost trust on a store with no
track record yet.

- The homepage advertised '0% Buyer protected' and '0/7 Customer Support'.
  CountUp treats any value starting with digits as a count, so the fixed claims
  '100%' and '24/7' animated up from zero on first paint — stating the exact
  opposite of the label. Counts now opt in explicitly, and ratios can never
  animate regardless of caller.
- The stats block showed '0 Happy Customers' and '0 Orders Delivered' before
  the first sale. A count is now only rendered once it is real, and the block is
  topped up with promises that hold on day one.
- The empty 'What Our Customers Say' card announced that nobody had bought yet;
  it is …
Clean authorization: strictly validates document ownership against authenticated session user ID.

* Fix AdSense low-value-content rejection: unblock exam content from crawlers

ExamDetailPage rendered a login-gated placeholder (identical hardcoded
stat boxes on every page) to anonymous visitors, which is what Googlebot
sees since the site is statically exported with no live session at build

Screen recording showed the OAuth flow reaching Google's account chooser
successfully (confirming the Client ID/redirect URI fix was correct), then
failing with "No authorization code received" immediately after redirect
back to /auth/google/callback.

Root cause: this page is statically exported, so next/router's router.query
starts empty and is only populated with the URL's query string after
client-side hydration parses it. The effect that reads searchParams.get

parsing the query string before deciding no code was received. Also fixed

### The credential is the agent's, never the dashboard's

A dashboard connection row bound to an agent stores the agent's **name for it** and
nothing else: no host, no username, no password. The job says *"run `inventory_sync` on
`dc1-vcenter`"* and the agent resolves the rest from its own
[`connections.yaml`](../examples/remote-agent/connections.example.yaml).

That is the difference between this and a proxy. Shipping credentials in the job
envelope would put a standing vCenter administrator password in the dashboard's
database, in every job payload, in the agent's memory — and, because **envelopes are
signed rather than encrypted**, in the logs of any TLS-inspecting proxy in between. The
[whole feature is sold](#behind-a-tls-inspecting-proxy) on the opposite property.

The cost is two files joined by a string, and a typo in either yields
`unknown connection 'dc1-vcenter'`. The connection form mitigates that by offering an
agent picker rather than a free-text uuid.

### Three grants, all required

Nothing runs unless all three agree, and they belong to different people:

| Grant | Who owns it | Where |
|---|---|---|
| this agent may run `agent_hypervisor` | the dashboard operator | Agents page |
| this verb is allowed on this connection | **you** | `policy.yaml` → `connections:` |
| this connection exists, with a credential | **you** | `connections.yaml` |

Withhold any one and nothing happens. A refusal from the second or third arrives in

not pretend to.

feat(agents): fetch hypervisor credentials just-in-time, sealed per fetch

An agent-bound hypervisor connection kept its credential on the agent host, in a
plaintext connections.yaml. Anyone who could read files there -- root, the docker
group, a backup, a copied volume -- had a standing vCenter/Proxmox administrator
password: offline, permanent, and silent, because a file read is not an event
anybody sees.

The credential can now live on the dashboard instead, and the agent fetches it for
each job over the poll channel it already has. Opt-in per connection, and the opt-in
is in the CUSTOMER's file (`dashboard_secret: true`), not a dashboard toggle -- a
credential set on the Connections page does nothing until their file says so.

This inverts a deliberate, documented trade, so the invariant is narrowed rather
than dropped: the dashboard may hold the SECRET, never the TARGET. `host` and
`username` are still always the agent's, because those aim the connection -- a
dashboard able to set `host` could redirect the agent's authenticated session at an
endpoint of its choosing and harvest the credential on first use.

With `ps_account://<id>` as the connection's secret_ref, neither side holds a
standing password: the dashboard checks one out of Password Safe per job, checks it
back in, and rotates it on release.

Sealed, not merely transported. `agent_signing` bought authentication the hard way
because an inspecting corporate proxy reads request bodies; the same proxy reads
response bodies, so the credential is encrypted at the application layer (ephemeral
X25519 -> HKDF-SHA256 -> AES-256-GCM, `services/agent_sealing`). The recipient key
is generated per fetch and rides in the already-signed request body, so there is no
new column, no enrolment change, no rotation protocol, and no decryption key on the
host to steal and use against traffic captured earlier. The AAD binds agent, job and
connection ref and is rebuilt from trusted state on both sides, never transmitted --
the ref most of all, since without it a credential can be relabelled as one for a
connection pointing somewhere else.

Notable details, each with the reason in the code:

* The connection is derived from the job row, never chosen by the request. Without
  that, a stolen agent identity enumerates every credential the dashboard holds.
* `statuses=("running",)`, not the WINDING_DOWN default: a cancelled job may still
  log and complete, but gets no fresh credential.
* The reply key is validated BEFORE the credential is obtained, so a malformed
  request cannot burn Password Safe checkouts and rotations.
* Release is ref-counted. ConflictOption=reuse hands concurrent jobs one request id,
  so releasing per job would rotate the password under a live sibling.
* The sweeper, not the completion hook, is the authority: reconcile_stale_jobs writes
  `failed` inline and never reaches complete_job, which is exactly the killed-agent
  case that matters most.
* Fetched credentials are scrubbed from everything outbound. `execute` was shipping
  raw `str(exc)[:1000]` into the job row, which is the only text a failed job renders,
  and an arbitrary library's exception message can carry a credential.
* Gated at enqueue on the agent version, so a 2.0 agent cannot fall through to a
  password the operator just deleted, send an empty one, and lock the account out.

Also fixes, in passing: `ps_api_service._checkout` left a request open when a
pending approval refused the credential, holding the account's concurrent-request
slot for the whole duration; and `update()` let an admin set `host` on an agent-bound
row, which `create()` had stripped -- harmless while nothing read it, not harmless now.

Two doc claims were already stale before this change and are corrected: "the agent
holds no target credentials" broke when hypervisor brokering shipped, and the roadmap
listed agent-side Password Safe checkout as future work when it has been live.

Tests: 67 new assertions across four files, incl. each AAD field bound independently,
the small-order key case, cross-implementation seal/open, IDOR, the shared-request
ref count, and release-on-reap. The two tests that encoded the old invariant failed
as expected and were split/extended rather than silenced.

fix(ci): a rotated BYOD token must announce a skip, not red the deploy

The BYOD smoke suite runs against a third-party Supabase project named only by
two secrets — a project this pipeline never deploys to. `deploy.yml` documents
it as opt-in coverage whose contract is "an absent configuration self-skips" and
"only a real BYOD assertion failure fails the step", but a token that project no
longer accepts was neither, and it failed the step: every BYOD test errors with
MCP -32001, reddening smoke-preview and, through the lockstep gate, blocking the
production deploy of an unrelated change (run 32217158749, failing since
2026-08-18 19:13Z).

Probe the credential once before the suite is collected and widen exactly one
outcome into an announced skip: JSON-RPC -32001. That code is emitted in one
place (the edge's missing/invalid/rotated-token branch) and mcp-authz-status
already pins that every authorization denial uses JSONRPC_FORBIDDEN instead, so
it cannot mean anything but "this project does not accept this token". Every
other outcome — an HTTP error, an unreachable host, a 5xx, a wrong answer — still
fails the suite, so no regression in the memory tools can hide behind it.

The skip is loud (console + a ::warning:: annotation naming the rotation) so
lost coverage is visible rather than silent, and two drift guards pin that the
escape hatch stays narrow.

fix(security): close account takeover, IDOR and injection paths

Each of these was verified exploitable against a running instance before the
change and verified closed after.

- /api/reset-password rewrote any account's password given only an email
  address. The OTP flow was decorative: verify-otp deleted its own record, so
  nothing server-side proved verification had happened. The record now carries
  a `verified` flag that reset-password requires and consumes, single-use and
  bounded by the existing 5-minute TTL.

- Request-body values reached Mongoose filters unchecked, so {"$gt":""} as an
  email matched an arbitrary user without knowing any address. Added string
  type guards, which also cover the array form that mongoose's own
  sanitizeFilter does not catch.

- /view-{cardio,dia,lung}-report returned any user's clinical record by id
  along with the owner's real name. The handlers already resolved the owner
  and never compared it to the caller. Ownership is derived from the User
  array rather than a userId column because LungData has no such field.

- /api/job-status and /api/job-result had no auth at all, and BullMQ assigns
  sequential integer ids, so results were enumerable. Jobs now carry the
  submitting userId and both routes verify it. Raw Python stderr is no longer
  returned to the client.

- /api/signup accepted an attacker-supplied groupId, and switch-profile then
  minted a token for any member of that group without a password. groupId is
  no longer read from the body.

- The bcrypt hash shipped to clients on signin, signup, switch-profile and
  GET /. password is now select:false and every response is projected.

- The five auth middlewares answered a bad token with 500 and jwt's raw
  message. They return 401 with a generic message. req.user is deliberately
  left as a bare string in authUser: eight call sites depend on that shape.

- GET / had no try/catch. Express 4 does not catch async rejections and Node
  defaults to --unhandled-rejections=throw, so one transient query failure
  killed the API process. Both clients hit this endpoint on startup.

- Added a 404 handler and a global error handler. Mongoose validation errors
  now return 400 instead of 500, so the UI stops reporting a user's typo as a
  server fault, and stack traces no longer leak.

fix(events): unstick cross-tenant organisers and admins from event check-in

The last corner of the bug class cleared by 5373940c8: four ACTOR lookups
on the attendance path resolved the acting user with `AND tenant_id = ?`
against the event's tenant, so a platform admin, network admin, or the
event's own cross-tenant organiser was refused check-in / attendance
marking with event_attendance_authorization_denied:

- EventService::attendanceActor() (markAttended + bulk marking)
- EventsController::attendanceActor() (the v2 check-in endpoints)
- the persisted-actor re-read inside EventAttendanceService::record()
- the persisted-actor re-read inside EventAttendanceService::transition()

Fixing only the outer attendanceActor() would have changed nothing: the
service re-read the actor with the same predicate and refused again.

Root Cause: the acting user's own identity lookup was tenant-scoped. Auth
is global in this codebase; only resources are tenant-scoped.

Prevention: the actor resolves by authenticated id alone (no IDOR risk —
the id comes from the authenticated session); authority is still decided
by EventPolicy::manageAttendance against the tenant-scoped event, and
event/attendee/registration lookups stay tenant-scoped. Six regression
tests in EventAttendanceCrossTenantActorTest assert the services directly
(Sanctum::actingAs masks cross-tenant behaviour); the three positive cases
were verified to fail against the old predicate, and the stranger,
suspended-actor and foreign-event guards hold under both versions.

EventsController::legacyRegistrationActor() carries the same predicate but
has different authorization semantics (self-registration, not policy-gated
management) — deliberately left out of scope, flagged for its own review.

fix: OVHcloud's zero-priced rows are safety classifiers, and the row read like that was the offer

The README's first command points at OVHcloud because it is the only keyless
entry here, and a reader who follows the link lands on the catalog page, sees a
price beside gpt-oss-120b and a $0 beside Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B, and concludes the
list is advertising a guard model as free Qwen3. The row invited that reading:
it listed the families as `qwen3` and `gpt-oss` while its own limits sentence
said the only zero-priced rows were the two Qwen3Guard models, the whispers and
stable-diffusion-xl.

The price column is not this row's offer. OVHcloud documents the lane it is
listed for, which nothing here had quoted: "Anonymous: 2 requests per minute,
per IP and per model. Authenticated with an API access key: 400 requests per
minute, per PCI project and per model" — help.ovhcloud.com's AI Endpoints
getting-started page, now in source_urls. Those prices are what an
authenticated project pays.

Measured against the endpoint on 2026-08-19 with no Authorization header:
gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct all
answer 200 with a real completion; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B answered 429 on six
attempts spread over four minutes and is therefore claimed nowhere. So the
families are now gpt-oss, qwen3.6 and qwen3-coder — the generations the lane
actually serves, named precisely enough that Qwen3Guard cannot be mistaken for
them — and the callable ids are the three that answered.

The 429 itself needed saying. Two requests per minute is what pays for the
missing key, and an unexplained rate-limit error on the one command the page
promises reads as a stale list. `_quickstart` now carries the entry's api note
onto the page under the curl, so the caveat lives in the registry beside the
evidence for it rather than typed into the template, where it would outlive the
entry it describes.

### Added

- **Direct-to-S3 song upload via presigned URLs.** The API no longer accepts audio as `byte[]` or
  `MultipartFile`. `POST /api/v1/albums/{albumId}/songs` (`ROLE_ARTIST`) validates content type
  and size (max 500 MB), persists song metadata, and returns short-lived (10 min) presigned PUT
  URL(s). Files larger than 100 MB receive S3 multipart part URLs. The client uploads directly to
  S3; `POST /api/v1/albums/{albumId}/songs/{songId}/confirm` verifies the object (or completes
  multipart with part ETags). Domain `SongStoragePort` exposes `generateUploadUrl` /
  `confirmUpload` with pure value objects (`SongUploadCommand`, `PresignedUploadResult`,
  `ConfirmUploadCommand`). AWS SDK v2 stays in `S3SongStorageAdapter`.
- **Twelve-Factor compliance hardening.**
  - Factor 3 — production config contract: `application-prod.yaml` binds every env-specific value
    from env vars and `ProdConfigValidator` (prod profile only) aborts startup with a clear message

### Fixed

- **Playlist IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) eliminated.** All four playlist mutation
  use cases (`UpdatePlaylistDetailsService`, `DeletePlaylistService`, `AddSongToPlaylistService`,
  `RemoveSongFromPlaylistService`) now enforce ownership via `PlaylistOwnershipGuard`, which throws
  `ForbiddenException` (mapped to HTTP 403) when the authenticated user is not the playlist owner.
  The `currentUserId` is injected from the security context in every controller mutation path — never
  trusted from the request body. Covered by unit tests (per-service forbidden/not-found cases) and
  E2E A-versus-B tests in `PlaylistFlowIT`.
- **DynamoDB empty-page crashes.** `findByProfileEmail` used `page.items().get(0)` and the
  playlist/like queries used `iterator().next()`; all now stream empty pages safely
  (`IndexOutOfBoundsException` / `NoSuchElementException` on fresh tables).

  Redis host from env vars in real deployments).

+1.9.3 - `unreleased`

+- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
+  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could
+  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
+  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
+  real certificate belonging to another user. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
+  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``

+  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
+  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request, closing the
+  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

Issue #2993. Two gates need the same answer: "which post-image lines did this
change actually touch?" The mypy gate in ``scripts/validation/git_hook_policy.py``
answered it first (``_parse_changed_lines``); the ruff gate in
``scripts/ci/ruff_ratchet.py`` linted whole touched files instead, so a
contributor editing a clean line inherited every pre-existing finding in the
file. This module is the single authoritative representation of the parsing so
the two gates cannot drift.

``scripts/validation/git_hook_policy.py::_parse_changed_lines`` at commit
4f5a12c::

Strict meta channel recognition in server

This addresses a security vulnerability affecting user-added extensions
that implement access control for channels. These extensions typically
work by checking incoming messages whose channel is `/meta/subscribe`
and then performing some authentication routine before allowing the
message through.

However, the Server parses channels in a way that means any channel
namespaced under `/meta/subscribe` will also work as a subscription
request. For example if the client sends a message to the channel
`/meta/subscribe/x`, that will bypass most authentication extensions but
will still be interpreted by the server as a subscription request, and
the client will be subscribed to the requested channel. The client has
thus bypassed the user's access control policy.

Here we prevent this by using a strict equality check; only messages
whose channel is exactly `/meta/subscribe` will be interpreted as
subscription requests. The same pattern is applied to all other meta
channels.

fix(gate-8): judge how the CALLER consumes the null, not the shape alone (#506)

gate-8 matches `catch (\Throwable) { return null; }` in a method whose name
says it resolves authorization. That shape is only a fail-open when the
CALLER treats null as "check skipped" — which is what decidesk#45 was:

    $auth = $this->getAuthorizationService();
    if ($auth !== null) {            // null SKIPS the check
        $auth->assertMayApprove($user);
    }

The opposite consumption is fail-CLOSED and is not a defect at all:

    if ($this->authorizeEmployee($id) === null) {
        return new JSONResponse([...], Http::STATUS_NOT_FOUND);   // null DENIES
    }

Measured on hrmq: 13 findings, ALL THIRTEEN of the second shape, across the
AvgDsr / Comp / Document / Expense / Interview / Leave / Loonbeslag / Offer /
Payroll / Roster controllers. The gate was asking an app to make its
authorization weaker in order to satisfy an authorization gate.

Narrowing the catch was not an escape either, which is why this belongs in
the checker rather than in the apps: OpenRegister's ObjectService::find()
throws a bare `Exception` when an object is missing, so for these resolvers
the catch IS the not-found path. There is no narrower exception to name.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

  - Restructuring the apps so `return null` sits outside the catch. That
    games the regex without changing one byte of behaviour.
  - Adding a prose exclusion marker. A security gate that can be switched
    off by apologising to it has stopped being a gate.

HOW IT DECIDES

`_classify_callers()` looks at every `$this-><resolver>(` in the same file,
both the inline form (`if ($this->r(...) === null)`) and the
assign-then-test form (`$x = $this->r(); ... if ($x === null)`), and:

  * `!== null` ANYWHERE wins and the finding stands — one skip-shaped caller
    is the defect no matter how many deny-shaped ones sit beside it;
  * only when at least one caller denies and none skip is the finding
    suppressed;
  * no classifiable caller means the finding STANDS. A resolver whose
    consumption cannot be seen is exactly the one to keep reporting, and it
    is why every pre-existing fixture — none of which has a caller — is
    still reported unchanged.

EVIDENCE

  * All 17 existing assertions still pass, including the decidesk#45 one.
  * Four new assertions, in both directions: deny-shaped caller suppressed,
    decidesk#45 still reported, one skip among denies still reported, and
    no-caller still reported.
  * hrmq: 13 findings -> 0.
  * All 50 gate self-tests pass.

One thing this evidence does NOT show, stated plainly: a before/after sweep
across the other 15 apps found no difference, but their gate-8 baseline is
ZERO, so that comparison had nothing to detect. It establishes that no other
app has a finding to lose — not that the change is behaviour-preserving
there.

class APIKeyCookie(APIKeyBase):
    """
    API key authentication using a cookie.

    This defines the name of the cookie that should be provided in the request with
    the API key and integrates that into the OpenAPI documentation. It extracts
    the key value sent in the cookie automatically and provides it as the dependency
    result. But it doesn't define how to set that cookie.

    ## Usage

    Create an instance object and use that object as the dependency in `Depends()`.

    The dependency result will be a string containing the key value.

    ## Example

    ```python
    from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
    from fastapi.security import APIKeyCookie

    app = FastAPI()

    cookie_scheme = APIKeyCookie(name="session")

    @app.get("/items/")
    async def read_items(session: str = Depends(cookie_scheme)):

def login(form_data: Annotated[OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict, Depends()]):
        data = {}
        data["scopes"] = []
        for scope in form_data.scopes:
            data["scopes"].append(scope)
        if form_data.client_id:
            data["client_id"] = form_data.client_id
        if form_data.client_secret:
            data["client_secret"] = form_data.client_secret
        return data
    ```

    Note that for OAuth2 the scope `items:read` is a single scope in an opaque string.
    You could have custom internal logic to separate it by colon characters (`:`) or
    similar, and get the two parts `items` and `read`. Many applications do that to
    group and organize permissions, you could do it as well in your application, just
    know that it is application specific, it's not part of the specification.

    grant_type: the OAuth2 spec says it is required and MUST be the fixed string "password".
        This dependency is strict about it. If you want to be permissive, use instead the
        OAuth2PasswordRequestForm dependency class.
    username: username string. The OAuth2 spec requires the exact field name "username".
    password: password string. The OAuth2 spec requires the exact field name "password".
    scope: Optional string. Several scopes (each one a string) separated by spaces. E.g.

Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

Hash token before storing it in Swift

Swauth uses token value as object name. Object names are logged in proxy
and object servers. Anybody with access to proxy/object server logs can
see token values. Attacker can use this token to access user's data in
Swift store. Instead of token, hashed token (with HASH_PATH_PREFIX and
HASH_PATH_SUFFIX) is used as object name now.

explanation:
fix: enforce feature permissions on the legacy chat-features block (image_generation, web_search) (#26703)

The legacy features block in process_chat_payload honoured client-supplied features.image_generation and features.web_search flags and dispatched to the image generation/edit provider and the web-search provider without re-checking the per-user permission that the direct /images routes and the native function-calling path enforce. A user denied features.image_generation or features.web_search could still trigger billable server-side image generation or web search via POST /api/chat/completions with params.function_calling set to legacy. Gate both branches on admin-or-has_permission before invoking chat_image_generation_handler / chat_web_search_handler, matching the existing code_interpreter gate, so a forged flag from an unpermitted user is ignored. Normal completions and permitted users are unaffected.

NovelTea is a self-hosted, offline-first long-form writing app, Scrivener-shaped: a binder tree, document snapshots, labels/statuses, custom metadata, saved/smart collections, and compile presets. Clients are web, Tauri (Windows/macOS), and iOS. Every client keeps a full local replica and works fully disconnected.

Copyright Anthony Carlascio. This repo is the **open core** under Elastic License 2.0; commercial features live in a separate private repo (see Editions).

- **`WireEnumTest`** drives off the enum constants themselves, so a new value is covered the moment it is added: round-tripping, unique lowercase wire forms, case and whitespace tolerance, and empty (never an exception) for null, blank, unknown and injection-shaped input.
- **`EnumSchemaAlignmentTest`** reads the allowed values out of `pg_constraint` and compares them to the enum, then writes every value to the real table. The enum and the CHECK constraint are two declarations of one fact in different languages; nothing but this keeps them honest. Add a value to one and not the other and it fails, naming the constraint.

## Compile

`packages/compile` turns ProseMirror documents into the formats Core ships (`txt`, `md`, `html`). `ExportProvider` on the Java side reports the same boundary; a commercial module contributes the remaining formats by supplying another implementation, and Core must keep working with only its own provider present.

### binder_item

The tree structure — folders, documents, trash. This is the Scrivener "binder."

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

| type | enum | `folder` \| `document` \| `trash` |
| title | text | |
| order_index | float | fractional indexing — lets you reorder/insert without rewriting siblings *(superseded — see A4)* |
| icon | text, nullable | optional custom icon (Scrivener-style) |
| deleted_at | timestamptz, nullable | soft delete — needed for sync tombstones |
| version | bigint | monotonic, incremented on every change |
| updated_by_device_id | uuid | for conflict attribution |

| id | uuid | same as binder_item.id, or separate FK — recommend same id for simplicity |
| content | jsonb | ProseMirror doc JSON |
| word_count | int | derived, cached for fast binder display |
| synopsis | text, nullable | the Scrivener index-card text |
| notes | text, nullable | document notes (rich text or plain) |
| version | bigint | incremented per content save |
| updated_at | timestamptz | |

### snapshot

Manual or auto point-in-time captures of a document's content (Scrivener's snapshot feature).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### label / status

Scrivener-style metadata taxonomies, per project.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### custom_metadata_field + custom_metadata_value

For arbitrary principal-defined metadata (Scrivener's custom meta-data pane). Field defs at the project level, values keyed per binder_item.

### collection

- Each entity carries a version integer, bumped on every write.
- Client pushes a batch: {entity, base_version, new_data} for each locally-changed record since last sync.
- Server accepts if base_version matches current server version (no one else changed it since the client last knew about it). Otherwise it's a conflict.
- On conflict for document content: don't try to merge rich text — create a sibling binder_item titled "<original title> (Conflicted Copy, <device>, <timestamp>)" containing the client's version, and let the principal manually reconcile. This mirrors Dropbox/Scrivener'
explanation:
Allowlist link schemes, sweep every route for IDOR, drop product names

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs
escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative
references, normalising away case, whitespace and control characters first so
JaVaScRiPt: and an embedded tab do not slip past, and failing closed on schemes
nobody has listed. An unsafe link loses its anchor, keeps its text, and warns.
Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

IdorSweepTest enumerates every route from the handler mapping and drives each
one with a stranger's token. Routes naming another account's resource must not
answer 2xx; caller-scoped collections may, but must not contain the victim's
data; nothing may answer 500; and the victim's project must be unchanged
afterwards. Reading the mapping rather than a hand-written list means a new
controller method that forgets its authorization check fails immediately.

Removes third-party product names from tracked files, replacing them with
descriptions of the behaviour they referred to.

190 Java and 95 Node tests green. Verified by mutation: making the ownership
check pass for everyone turns the sweep red.

[MERGE] Recupera auditoria de seguranca da VPS descartada por push --force

RECUPERACAO DE TRABALHO PERDIDO.

O commit eaea83b (VPS, 16/08 22:34 UTC) foi apagado do main por um
`git push -f`. Este merge o traz de volta.

Como aconteceu: o pull desta maquina foi em 09/08 17:55, trazendo aca9ffa.
A VPS commitou eaea83b UMA SEMANA DEPOIS, em 16/08. O branch local nunca
soube dele; o push foi recusado por historico divergente e o -f mandou
sobrescrever. Os dois ramos partiam da mesma base (aca9ffa).

O QUE VOLTOU (62 arquivos)
- SQL injection corrigido em SendMail.ts e queues.ts (arquivos DIFERENTES
  dos que a auditoria daqui corrigiu — as duas se complementam)
- sequelize 5.22.5 -> 6.37.8, sequelize-typescript 1.1.0 -> 2.1.6,
  sequelize-cli 5.5.1 -> 6.6.5, com 77 erros de tipo corrigidos e bugs
  reais expostos pela tipagem estrita (guard morto em timeUseBotQueues,
  paginacao de Tags/ContactLists, campos fantasma em .update())
- ~10 dependencias com CVE: axios 1.7.9 -> 1.19.0 (~15 CVEs), jsonwebtoken
  8.5.1 -> 9.0.3, multer, nodemailer, puppeteer, baileys rc9 -> rc14
- bcrypt de custo 8 para 12
- SSH endurecido, fail2ban, ufw; backups com umask 077
- CSP + Permissions-Policy no nginx do frontend
- nginx/sites/crm.conf passa a ser versionado

RESOLUCAO DOS CONFLITOS (2 arquivos, ambos de dependencia)
- jsonwebtoken: 9.0.3 (versao da VPS vence — e correcao de CVE)
- lodash + @types/lodash: mantidos (nossos)
- long: mantido (deles)
- package-lock.json: regenerado a partir do lockfile da VPS

BUG QUE O AUTO-MERGE CRIOU E FOI CORRIGIDO
O git juntou `server_tokens off;` dos DOIS lados em nginx.conf. Diretiva
duplicada no mesmo contexto faz o nginx recusar a config inteira e nao
subir — teria derrubado o site no deploy. Duplicata removida e validado
com `nginx -t` em container: syntax is ok.

VERIFICACAO
- npm ci com lockfile mesclado: 1109 pacotes, limpo
- tsc --noEmit: limpo (o modulo de tokens escrito contra sequelize 5 e
  compativel com o 6 sem alteracao)
- npm run build: limpo
- sequelize db:migrate com CLI 6: as 3 migrations novas lidas sem erro
- nginx -t: ok
- Suite COMPLETA: 60 suites, exit code 0
- Conferido que os fixes das DUAS auditorias sobrevivem lado a lado:
  resolveCompanyId (IDOR), parseReportParams (SQLi relatorios), XSS do
  LocationPreview/LogPlw e CSP com nonce daqui; SQLi do SendMail/queues e
  CSP do nginx de la.

LICAO REGISTRADA
Nunca usar `git push -f` neste repositorio. Com commits vindo desta
maquina e da VPS, force push apaga trabalho de quem commitou por ultimo.
Push recusado se resolve com pull + merge, como feito aqui.

Fix Skydropx webhook auth: every event was rejected before reaching the code

Skydropx sends the shared token as "Authorization: Bearer <token>", which
Supabase's gateway parses as a JWT and rejects with
UNAUTHORIZED_INVALID_JWT_FORMAT, so the function never ran. Redeploy with
verify_jwt=false and note the flag in the file header so a future deploy
does not silently reinstate it.

The token comparison also assumed a bare secret, so even past the gateway
"Bearer <token>" would never match. Now strips the prefix, accepts the
alternate x-skydropx-signature header, and compares in constant time.

Payload parsing handled only the flat v1 shape; PRO also sends JSON:API
({data:{type:"packages",attributes:{...}}}), so lookups now search
attributes, data and root, with a fallback match on skydropx_shipment_id
when no tracking number is present.

Status map was missing PICKED_UP, LAST_MILE, DELIVERY_ATTEMPT, PENDING,
RETURNED and the single-L "CANCELED" that Skydropx actually sends. Order
transitions are now rank-guarded so a late event cannot walk a delivered
order back to shipped. Unknown shipments return 200 instead of 404 so
Skydropx does not retry an event that will never match.

The admission contract for epic [#801](https://github.com/nathanjohnpayne/gaycruisebingo/issues/801), consumed by every other child in it. It defines what a membership record is, where it lives, who may write it, the single predicate the two rules files transcribe, and the per-Event switch that lets enforcement land dark. It changes no rule and ships no UI: `firestore.rules`, `storage.rules` and `functions/**` are deliberately untouched, so that #803–#809 start from a settled shape instead of five divergent ones.

**Status is `proposed`, not `accepted`, and that is a deliberate signal.** The parts the code forces are settled and safe to build against — the invariant, the path, the single-`get()` constraint, the document shape, the predicate, the budget, and the enforcement switch. Two of the epic's open decisions are genuinely product (§ Decisions, D2/D8) and are recorded here as options rather than answers; D5 and D-A were ruled on by the owner 2026-08-18 and are now answers. Downstream tickets may implement everything under § Contract today; under § Decisions, the three the owner has ruled on (D5, D9, D-A) are commitments and the rest are not.

## The invariant

**A gate the reader can satisfy by writing its own admission record is not a gate.**

Every candidate record in the tree today is exactly that. `events/{eventId}/players/{uid}` is `allow create, update: if (isOwner(uid) || isAdmin(eventId)) && reshuffleCounterMonotonic()` (`firestore.rules:1007-1008`) with no membership precondition, so any signed-in account mints its own Player row under any Event id it knows and then satisfies any predicate keyed off that row. The same self-create shape exists at `items` (`:958-968`), `reshuffles` (`:1044-1053`), `proofs` (`:1202-1283`), `claims` (`:1305`), `markers` (`:1332-1337`), `doubts` (`:1351-1396`), `hearts` (`:1419-1456`) and `moments` (`:1466-1532`).

This is not a theoretical objection. [#844](https://github.com/nathanjohnpayne/gaycruisebingo/issues/844), filed from PR #838's review, reached it independently and from the other direction: `resolveAbuseEscalation` (`functions/src/bugReports.ts`) gates an admin alert on the reporter holding a Player document, and Codex correctly observed that the check is a fact the client asserts rather than one the platform knows. That issue's own conclusion — *"Some Event-scoped notion of legitimate participation that a client cannot mint"* — is what this spec specifies, and its first listed candidate ("a server-written membership fact — join goes through a callable that records something clients cannot write") is the shape adopted below.

The in-tree precedent for a record whose value depends on clients being unable to author it is `hostnames/{host}`: `allow get: if true; allow list: if false; allow create, update, delete: if false` (`firestore.rules:624-628`) — written only by the Admin SDK. Membership follows it exactly.

## Glossary

**Membership** — the organizer-issued record that a User is admitted to one Event. One document per (Event, User), non-self-writable, carrying the grant's provenance and its revocation. It is a *record*, not a

explanation:
Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

def build_auth_provider() -> MultiAuth:
    """Compose Okta OIDC + agent-jwt JWT verification via FastMCP MultiAuth.

    MultiAuth tries the Okta OIDCProxy first (interactive users), then the
    JWTVerifier (programmatic agent-jwt tokens). The two paths are fully
    independent.

    Required environment variables:
        AGENT_JWT_SECRET: Shared HS256 secret for verifying agent-jwt tokens.
        (Plus everything required by ``build_okta_provider``.)
    """
    return MultiAuth(
        server=build_okta_provider(),
        verifiers=[
            JWTVerifier(
                public_key=require_env("AGENT_JWT_SECRET"),
                algorithm="HS256",
                issuer=AGENT_JWT_ISSUER,
            ),
        ],
