NovelTea is a self-hosted, offline-first long-form writing app, Scrivener-shaped: a binder tree, document snapshots, labels/statuses, custom metadata, saved/smart collections, and compile presets. Clients are web, Tauri (Windows/macOS), and iOS. Every client keeps a full local replica and works fully disconnected.

Copyright Anthony Carlascio. This repo is the **open core** under Elastic License 2.0; commercial features live in a separate private repo (see Editions).

- **`WireEnumTest`** drives off the enum constants themselves, so a new value is covered the moment it is added: round-tripping, unique lowercase wire forms, case and whitespace tolerance, and empty (never an exception) for null, blank, unknown and injection-shaped input.
- **`EnumSchemaAlignmentTest`** reads the allowed values out of `pg_constraint` and compares them to the enum, then writes every value to the real table. The enum and the CHECK constraint are two declarations of one fact in different languages; nothing but this keeps them honest. Add a value to one and not the other and it fails, naming the constraint.

## Compile

`packages/compile` turns ProseMirror documents into the formats Core ships (`txt`, `md`, `html`). `ExportProvider` on the Java side reports the same boundary; a commercial module contributes the remaining formats by supplying another implementation, and Core must keep working with only its own provider present.

### binder_item

The tree structure — folders, documents, trash. This is the Scrivener "binder."

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

| type | enum | `folder` \| `document` \| `trash` |
| title | text | |
| order_index | float | fractional indexing — lets you reorder/insert without rewriting siblings *(superseded — see A4)* |
| icon | text, nullable | optional custom icon (Scrivener-style) |
| deleted_at | timestamptz, nullable | soft delete — needed for sync tombstones |
| version | bigint | monotonic, incremented on every change |
| updated_by_device_id | uuid | for conflict attribution |

| id | uuid | same as binder_item.id, or separate FK — recommend same id for simplicity |
| content | jsonb | ProseMirror doc JSON |
| word_count | int | derived, cached for fast binder display |
| synopsis | text, nullable | the Scrivener index-card text |
| notes | text, nullable | document notes (rich text or plain) |
| version | bigint | incremented per content save |
| updated_at | timestamptz | |

### snapshot

Manual or auto point-in-time captures of a document's content (Scrivener's snapshot feature).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### label / status

Scrivener-style metadata taxonomies, per project.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### custom_metadata_field + custom_metadata_value

For arbitrary caller-defined metadata (Scrivener's custom meta-data pane). Field defs at the project level, values keyed per binder_item.

### collection

- Each entity carries a version integer, bumped on every write.
- Client pushes a batch: {entity, base_version, new_data} for each locally-changed record since last sync.
- Server accepts if base_version matches current server version (no one else changed it since the client last knew about it). Otherwise it's a conflict.
- On conflict for document content: don't try to merge rich text — create a sibling binder_item titled "<original title> (Conflicted Copy, <device>, <timestamp>)" containing the client's version, and let the caller manually reconcile. This mirrors Dropbox/Scrivener's own

Allowlist link schemes, sweep every route for IDOR, drop product names

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs

fix(reprice): P1 — split !userId (401) from ownership check (403) on POST /:requestId/reprice (#1913)

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

## Test
server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId
  ✓ 401 guard sits BEFORE the first db.select() (no wasted round-trip)
  ✓ ownership check no longer folds !userId into the 403 branch

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  3 passed (3)

## Dependency
None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

## Do not merge
Per standing CEO directive.

fix: require message authorship for standard-channel message edit and delete (#27197)

The channel message update and delete handlers enforced authorship only on group and dm channels. On standard channels the else branch accepted any caller holding write access on the channel, so a member who could post could also edit or delete messages authored by other members. Because the update form binds content, data and meta, and the model layer never touches message.user_id, an edited message kept the original author's attribution, so another member's message could be rewritten under their name.

Write access on a channel is the capability to post, not a moderation capability, and the frontend gates the edit and delete controls on authorship (message.user_id === user.id, or admin) for every channel type. The group and dm branch already encodes this with an explicit authorship check. Apply the same rule to the standard branch: the caller must hold write access on the channel and be the message author, unless they are an admin. Pinning is unchanged, since it is exposed to every member by design.
Clean go function implementing properly authorized application logic.

docs: 2026-08-18 audit — fix what the docs got wrong, document what they never covered (#95)

* docs: point every config sample at config/authkit.ts

The provider reads `config.get('authkit')` and `node ace configure` writes
`config/authkit.ts`; 40 snippets across 23 pages told readers to edit a
`config/authkit_server.ts` that is never loaded.

* chore(renovate): stop the bot pinning engines.node to an exact version

renovate.json sets a global `rangeStrategy: "pin"`, which applies to the
`engines` depType as well: the bot rewrites a supported range like ">=20 <23"
into whatever single version it saw. Every consumer on any other Node then gets
an engine warning on install, and `engine-strict` fails outright. A packageRule
disabling the `engines` depType keeps the range a range.

* fix(authkit-server): declare onAccountExpirationWarning in MailHooks

authkit:expire-scan calls mail.onAccountExpirationWarning({ email,
expiresInDays }) through an untyped config read, so the hook existed at runtime
while being absent from the interface — no completion, no check on the payload,
and nothing for the docs to read.

* fix(authkit-testing): fakeAuthenticator covers the whole Authenticator surface

The client's Authenticator grew getUserOrFail() and toSharedProps();
FakeAuthenticatorLike did not, so the fake no longer type-checked against a
ctx.auth typed as Authenticator — the one thing it exists to do. A compile-time
assignment against the real class now fails the typecheck the moment the two
drift again.

* docs(authkit-server): the schema docblock lists all eight auto-managed tables

It named six and skipped auth_mfa and auth_session_revocations, so anyone
turning autoManage off sized the job wrong.

* chore: point homepage and bugs.url at the renamed repository

The repo is now DavideCarvalho/adonis-agora-authkit; repository.url followed the
rename but homepage and bugs.url still named adonis-authkit, so every published
manifest disagreed with itself and relied on GitHub's rename redirect.

* docs(authkit-server): drop the 'mirror the config' advice from AuthHostOptions

Policy options declared in defineConfig now lock the matching registerAuthHost
argument, so the docblocks were telling hosts to write code that gets ignored
with a boot warning.

* docs: rebuild the reference against the real export surface

The tables taught APIs that do not exist (Can, hasAppRole, resolveAppRoles), an
inverted config-lock precedence, a one-argument requireSudo, the wrong
onAccountExpirationWarning payload, an internal token prefix, and two of the
thirty doctor checks. Whole subsystems had no rows at all: resolveTokenRoles,
authMethods, routes, interactionRecovery, sudo, schema, accountLifecycle,
adonisAuth, the sudo-method SPI, config locks, trusted devices, the durable
subpath and the impersonation glue.

PasswordStrengthMeter is documented with its real props — it takes the password
and scores it, and never took a score.

* fix(authkit-server): SettingLockedError speaks English

The Admin API puts this message in the 423 response body, so it is read by
operators and integrators, not by the library.

* test(authkit-server): type-check the token-exchange specs, ratchet 292 -> 275

The two token-exchange specs landed with 6 net new type errors, pushing the
typecheck:tests count past its baseline — main has been red since. Typing the
response bodies, the resolved config and one findById parameter clears all 23
errors those two files carried, so the baseline drops to 275 instead of being
raised.

admin: { roles } gains the required enabled: false, which is what it already
resolved to.

* test(authkit-sdk): give the embedded-driver fake an issuer

Emailed links are now built from the resolved issuer rather than the request
host, so users.create walked into new URL(undefined) and threw. The fixture, not
the library, was missing a required field.

* fix(docs): register Steps, Tabs and Accordions with MDX

fumadocs-ui's default component map covers Card/Cards/Callout and the element
overrides only. Steps, Tabs and Accordions ship as separate entrypoints, so a
page using them renders in dev and then fails the production build with
"Expected component `Steps` to be defined".

* docs: give the config-lock system a page, and fix the inverted precedence

settings.mdx taught the opposite of the code: one rule, 'setting > lib default',
with the policy fields supposedly removed from defineConfig. In reality
declaring one of ten policy keys LOCKS the matching setting — getSetting reads
back null so the config value stands, and writes answer 423. None of
SettingLockedError, isSettingLocked, lockedSettingKeys, setLockedSettingKeys,
deriveLockedSettingKeys or POLICY_ROUTE_OPTIONS appeared on any page.

The new page covers both axes (config vs setting, and config vs registerAuthHost
argument), how to choose, what an operator sees when a lock holds, and the trap
where a key whose config type carries only infrastructure still locks its whole
policy.

settings.mdx also gains the two missing setting keys (roles_catalog,
key_rotation), the real eight-table schema list, and org-scoped settings.

* docs: fix the host-kit mirroring advice and the sudo surface

The 'Mirror them' callout told readers to repeat social/rateLimit/sudoMethods/
admin/adminApi in registerAuthHost; those arguments are now ignored with a boot
warning. host-kit also never stated the route-mounting convention, listed 4 of 9
AuthHostOptions fields, and had nothing on accountRoutes or interactionRecovery.

console-session called requireSudo(ctx) — the signature takes two required
arguments — and knew only the three legacy helpers, not the sudo-method SPI, the
derivation rules, or the account binding that stops a sudo grace surviving an
account switch.

* docs: rebuild the React pages against the real export surface

Can, hasAppRole, hasAnyAppRole, hasAllAppRoles and appRoles do not exist; the
real API is CanPermission/useCan and the global-role helpers. Three components
were documented with props they do not accept — PasswordStrengthMeter takes the
password and scores it, OrganizationSwitcher and OrganizationProfile take
neither allowCreate nor orgId — and InteractionForm's step union was missing
otpVerify.

Adds the three passkey tiers, useResource/jsonRequest, checkCan, heuristicScorer,
interactionUrls, the config layer, the keys hooks, the org member/invitation
hooks, and the three missing AuthkitProvider endpoints.

* docs: lead with registerOidcClient, and document the @adonisjs/auth integration

client.mdx still taught the three-step generatePkce/buildAuthorizeUrl/exchangeCode
dance that registerOidcClient exists to delete, hand-wrote the updateOrCreate
that lucidMirror ships, resolved the manager through the container instead of the
services/main singleton, and documented a resolveAppRoles option that does not
exist. The batteries-included back-channel path (backchannelLogout: { store },
lucidRevocationStore, BackchannelRevocationMiddleware) had no page at all — only
the manual SessionIndex.

The new adonis-auth page covers OidcRpGuard, authkitUserProvider, the
adonisAuth: { guard } key and authkitClientGuard: the feature that makes
ctx.auth.user, middleware.auth() and the Bouncer work natively, and which had
zero mentions.

* docs: document OTP login, passwordless signup, trusted devices and the real mail hooks

Email login codes (login.otp, the code/link selector, the attempt counter, the
pure helpers) and password-free public signup were undocumented, and their four
audit events were missing from events.mdx along with
organization.member_role_changed.

security.mdx documented onAccountExpirationWarning with a payload it never had,
omitted onSudoLink, onOrgInvitation and the mail.origin escape hatch, and
described rate limiting as off by default and needing to be mirrored into
registerAuthHost. trustedDevices had one line and none of its exports, nor the
rule that step-up always ignores the cookie.

Also drops an internal magic-link token prefix from passwordless.mdx.

* docs: document durable account lifecycle and the impersonation prerequisites

The word 'durable' appeared on no page: accountLifecycle: { durable: true } and
the whole /durable subpath were invisible, and compliance.mdx knew only the
synchronous cascade.

impersonation.mdx was missing the RP-side glue entirely, including the
prerequisite that decides whether it works at all — the RP must request
offline_access and call rememberRefreshToken at login, or impersonation dies
when the admin's access token expires. It also lacked the admin.impersonation
kill switch, and its callout implied the IdP does not authorize the actor. It
does.

* docs: complete the account-store, Admin API, SDK and testing surfaces

account-store documented 6 of the 12 exported capability guards. admin-api
reduced ten organization routes to a line of prose and tabulated neither the
settings group nor the key-rotation routes. sdk.mdx was missing keys.status/
keys.rotate and both direct driver factories. testing.mdx claimed the fake
exposes exactly what ctx.auth exposes, which stopped being true when the
Authenticator grew getUserOrFail and toSharedProps.

* docs: fix the dead changelog links, the package cards, the vault config and the console

All six changelog links pointed at a repository that 404s; they now point at the
real one, and the page covers all nine publishable packages instead of five. The
introduction omitted authkit-testing and the three vaults. keystore-vaults listed
the drivers without ever showing a config shape and leaked two internal symbols.

admin-console leaked a build path and a private controller, carried
release-note framing, documented a settings route surface that does not exist,
and never mentioned the admin.impersonation kill switch.

* docs: document resolveTokenRoles and stop teaching APIs that do not exist

getting-started, customizing-auth and byo-idp taught ctx.auth.hasAppRole(), a
resolveAppRoles client option and a Can component — none of which exist in any
package. AuthKit carries global roles; per-app authorization belongs to authz,
and the seam that makes an external authority the source of roles is
resolveTokenRoles, which had no page.

The 'protect a group of routes' recipe hand-wrote the auth_middleware and
silent_auth_middleware the client package already ships.

* docs: list config-locks and adonis-auth in the sidebar

* test(authkit-server): assert the lock error by class and code, not by prose

The spec matched SettingLockedError's message with a regex, so translating that
message broke it. The class, the code and the key are the contract; the sentence
is not.

    """The IdP authorize URL for a fresh login (response_type=code). `state` and `nonce` are the single-use
    server-minted values recorded in the state store; the IdP echoes `state` at the callback and binds
    `nonce` into the id_token."""

explanation:
W16-6 (#512): add PKCE + session-bound state to the OIDC RP; default the username claim to immutable sub

The OIDC RP (SHIPPED OFF BY DEFAULT) previously minted a server-side single-use
`state`/`nonce` but did NOT bind the state to the initiating browser and carried
no PKCE — so login-CSRF / authorization-code injection were live (docs/OIDC-RP.md
named both as the required follow-on before a UI landing page adopts the bearer).
It also defaulted SIGIL_OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM to the MUTABLE preferred_username,
letting an IdP-side rename steer the account mapping.

Fix (additive; OIDC stays off-by-default, byte-identical when disabled):

- PKCE (RFC 7636, S256). /api/oidc/login mints a high-entropy code_verifier,
  advertises only its S256 code_challenge in the authorize redirect, and holds
  the verifier server-side bound to the state. The token exchange sends the
  verifier; exchange_code REFUSES a blank one. An intercepted/injected code is
  useless without the initiating session's verifier.
- Session-bound state. /api/oidc/login sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax cookie
  (Path=/api/oidc) and binds sha256(cookie) into the state record. The callback
  recomputes the hash of the presented cookie and REFUSES a missing/mismatched
  one (constant-time). SameSite=Lax still rides the IdP's top-level GET redirect.
- Immutable username claim. SIGIL_OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM now defaults to `sub`
  (globally unique, IdP-stable). preferred_username/email are opt-in only.

Fail-closed discipline: an old marker lacking sid_hash/verifier resolves to a
blank -> refused (no new fail-open); the legitimate same-browser path completes.

OidcStateStore.issue now binds (nonce, verifier, sid_hash); consume returns an
OidcLoginRecord (was the bare nonce string). Callers: server callback + tests.

CI job over the whole apps/sigil/tests/ dir):

- test_callback_requires_session_bound_cookie_defeats_login_csrf  (NEGATIVE
  CONTROL: missing/mismatched cookie -> 401 no bearer; same browser -> 200)
- test_default_username_claim_is_immutable_sub
- test_login_sets_httponly_samesite_lax_session_cookie
- test_exchange_code_refuses_blank_pkce_verifier
- test_pkce_s256_matches_rfc7636_appendix_b_vector

fix: scope knowledge sync cleanup deletions to the target knowledge base (#26722)

POST /knowledge/{id}/sync/cleanup verified write access to the knowledge base in the URL but then acted on the caller-supplied file_ids and dir_ids without checking they belong to that knowledge base. A user with write access to any knowledge base could pass another knowledge base's directory id to delete its directory subtree and knowledge_file associations, or another file's id to drop its file-{file_id} vector collection. Fetch each directory and skip any whose knowledge_id does not match the URL id (matching the explicit directory-delete endpoint), and gate the per-file vector cleanup on Knowledges.has_file(id, file_id) so a foreign file id cannot trigger collection deletion. Legitimate same-knowledge-base cleanup is unchanged.

fix(cli): verify-scope-configuration could never authenticate — three stacked bugs (#2131)

* fix(cli): stop leaking DOTENV_PRIVATE_KEY, and stop reporting configured env as missing

Two bugs found by running the CLI diagnostics that #2124 had just unblocked —
they had been unrunnable since the dotenvx cutover, so nothing had exercised
them.

1. DOTENV_PRIVATE_KEY could survive loadDemoEnv (SELF-INFLICTED, in #2124).

bootstrapDotenvx resolves the key from the env object it is handed and applies
decrypted values to it, so the key has to be on process.env for the duration of
the call. It deletes the key itself on success — but NOT on its
"module_unavailable" early return, which fires when @dotenvx/dotenvx cannot be
required and happens before that cleanup.

Under server.js the key was set externally, so leaving it behind is a no-op and
the early return is harmless. loadDemoEnv INJECTS it, so on that path a private
key was left in process.env — inherited by every child process these CLIs spawn,
and several of them do spawn children. The header comment claimed "the key never
lands in process.env", which was simply false of Object.assign(process.env, ...).

Now the injection is wrapped in try/finally: an externally-supplied key is
restored exactly as it was, one we introduced is removed, on every path.

2. verify-act-claims reported a correctly configured exchanger as "(not set)".

It read only PINGONE_MCP_TOKEN_EXCHANGER_CLIENT_ID / AGENT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID.
docs/ENV.md declares PINGONE_TOKEN_EXCHANGER_CLIENT_ID canonical, that is the
name .env actually carries, and configStore treats all four as aliases for one
value (services/configStore.js ~1180). So the script printed "(not set)" on a
working system — a diagnostic that reports live config as missing is worse than
none, because it sends you looking for the wrong thing. It now uses the same
alias chain configStore does, and prints the real id.

Verified: 3 new tests cover the key lifecycle (success path, module_unavailable
early return, externally-supplied key preserved); 2 of them fail against the
pre-fix loader. tests/scripts + dotenvxBootstrap 47/47. verify-act-claims now
prints the configured client id instead of "(not set)".

* fix(cli): useCaseSweep reported '.env NOT found' on runs that had loaded it

The sweep's status line was computed from existsSync(__dirname/../.env) — one
guessed path — while the actual loading goes through loadDemoEnv, which resolves
the MAIN checkout's .env when run from a worktree (a worktree has no gitignored
.env of its own). So a run that had loaded every value correctly still printed
'demo_api_server/.env NOT found, env-pinned flags may read as off'.

That is the same disease as the manufactured failure the comment above it warns
about, inverted: a false warning on a correct result makes you distrust output
that was right, or go chasing a flag problem that does not exist. Confirmed
harmless-but-wrong: BLOCKED stays 77 either way, so the reads were always fine
and only the reporting lied.

Now derived from loadDemoEnv's return value — the paths it actually loaded — and
it names them. fs and path became unused with the existsSync check and are
removed.

scripts/extract-browser-token.js writes .env.test-tokens (key

CLI verifier did — so both told you to go log in again while a freshly

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): verify-scope-configuration could never authenticate — three stacked bugs

The script exited 1 with "PINGONE_MGMT_CLIENT_ID or PINGONE_MGMT_CLIENT_SECRET
not set" on an environment that has working Management API credentials. Peeling
that back found three defects in a row, each masking the next.

1. Credentials were looked up under one name only.

A PingOne Worker app IS the Management API client, and this environment has one
configured as PINGONE_WORKER_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET. The script read only the
PINGONE_MGMT_* pair, so it reported "not set" and told the operator to go create
a second Worker app in the console that was never needed.

Now resolved as a PAIR across PINGONE_MGMT / PINGONE_MANAGEMENT /
PINGONE_WORKER_TOKEN / PINGONE_WORKER. As a pair, deliberately: taking the id
from one prefix and the secret from another gives a mismatched pair that fails
as invalid_client, which reads as a bad secret rather than a bad pairing.
(configStore's chains at ~1106-1107 resolve the two independently and carry the
same latent hazard — noted in a comment, not changed here.)

PINGONE_ADMIN_* is excluded even though configStore's chain includes it. In this
environment that is "Demo AI App - Admin Login", a WEB_APP whose grants are
AUTHORIZATION_CODE / REFRESH_TOKEN / TOKEN_EXCHANGE with no CLIENT_CREDENTIALS
(verified via the PingOne API). Preferring it over the Worker produced
"unauthorized_client: Unsupported grant type: client_credentials" — an error
about the grant when the real mistake was picking a login app to do a
machine-to-machine call.

2. The token request body was malformed.

It was built by string concatenation and sent
scope=p1:read:resource p1:read:resource_scope with a RAW SPACE, which is invalid
in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. PingOne mis-parsed the request and
answered with errors about the AUTH METHOD and the GRANT TYPE, neither of which
was wrong. Now built with URLSearchParams.

3. One token-endpoint auth method was hardcoded.

A Worker's tokenEndpointAuthMethod is per-app config and nothing in .env records
which. Basic-only meant an app configured for POST failed as
"invalid_client: Unsupported authentication method" — right secret, wrong
envelope. Now tries the configured method and falls back once on an
invalid_client-shaped rejection, the same shape as demo_authz_server's
introspection fallback (introspect.authMethodFallback.test.js).

Verified live against env 01d89b06: authenticates, fetches 28 resources, 20
resources clean.

It also immediately found real drift, which is the point of the script: the
"Demo API" resource (enduser.ping.demo) is MISSING four scopes the SoT requires
— purchase:read, membership:read, payroll:read, identity:read. Confirmed against
scope-topology.json rather than trusting the script's expectation. NOT fixed
here: --fix mutates a live PingOne tenant, which is the operator's call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): --fix requested a read-only token, so it could never create a scope

Fourth defect in the same script. --fix POSTs new scopes via
/v1/environments/{env}/resources/{id}/scopes, but the token was always requested
with 'p1:read:resource p1:read:resource_scope' — read-only. The create would
have been refused by PingOne no matter how correct everything else was, so the
repair path the script advertises could not work.

--fix now requests p1:create:resource_scope in addition. The default audit run is
unchanged and stays read-only on purpose: an audit should not be able to write,
and asking for write on every run would leave the read path carrying permission
it never needs.

Verified: the read-only run is byte-identical in behaviour — authenticates,
28 resources, same single finding.

NOT verified: the --fix write path itself. Running it is a live PingOne tenant
mutation and was declined by this session's permission classifier, so the
p1:create:resource_scope assumption is reasoned from the PingOne scope naming
convention, not observed. Whoever runs it first should check that the token is
granted and the POST returns 201.

fix(reprice): P1 — split !userId (401) from ownership check (403) on POST /:requestId/reprice (#1913)

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

## Test
server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId
  ✓ 401 guard sits BEFORE the first db.select() (no wasted round-trip)
  ✓ ownership check no longer folds !userId into the 403 branch

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  3 passed (3)

## Dependency
None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

## Do not merge
Per standing CEO directive.

소셜 로그인은 각 제공사 개발자 등록이 필요해요. 이메일 로그인만으로도 개발은 계속 진행할 수 있으니 나중에 해도 됩니다.

### 3-0. 구글 (완료 — Supabase 기본 제공 Google provider 그대로 사용)

구글은 이메일/프로필이 "민감하지 않은 기본 스코프"라 카카오 같은 권한 제한이 없다. Supabase
기본 제공 Google provider를 그대로 쓰면 된다(커스텀 Edge Function 불필요).

1. **console.cloud.google.com** → 새 프로젝트 생성(사업자 필요 없음, 무료 — 결제 계정 등록도
   필요 없다)
2. **API 및 서비스 → OAuth 동의 화면**
   - 대상: **외부** 선택
   - 앱 이름/지원 이메일/개발자 연락처 이메일 입력 → 저장
   - "테스트" 상태로 시작됨(등록한 테스트 사용자만 로그인 가능) — 실제 서비스 오픈 전까지는
     이 상태로 개발 진행 가능
3. **사용자 인증 정보 → OAuth 클라이언트 만들기**
   - 애플리케이션 유형: **웹 애플리케이션**
   - 승인된 리디렉션 URI: Supabase 대시보드 → Authentication → Providers → **Google**의
     Callback URL을 복사해서 등록
     ```
     https://bxntqggkfwnhcczsbqtj.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback
     ```
4. 발급된 **클라이언트 ID**, **클라이언트 보안 비밀번호**를 그 자리에서 바로 복사(창을 닫으면
   보안 비밀번호는 다시 못 봄) → Supabase 대시보드 Google Provider 설정에 붙여넣고 Enable → Save

> **알려진 제약(수정 불가, 기능엔 영향 없음)**: 구글 로그인 동의 화면에 앱 이름 대신
> `xxxxx.supabase.co 서비스로 로그인`이 표시된다. Supabase의 공용 도메인을 거쳐 인증이
> 이뤄지는 구조상 발생하는 것으로, 구글의 "승인된 도메인"에는 본인이 소유·인증한 도메인만
> 등록 가능해 `supabase.co`를 직접 추가할 수 없다. Supabase 유료 플랜의 커스텀 도메인을
> 설정하거나, 카카오/네이버처럼 완전 커스텀 OAuth 흐름으로 전환해야 해결되며 실사용 서비스
> 오픈 시점에 재검토할 사항으로 남겨둔다.

### 3-1. 카카오 — Supabase 기본 제공 Kakao provider 사용 불가, 커스텀 Edge Function으로 구현 완료

> Supabase의 기본 제공 Kakao provider(`signInWithOAuth({ provider: "kakao" })`)는 서버 쪽에서
> `account_email` 스코프를 무조건 같이 요청한다. 이 프로젝트의 카카오 앱은 이메일 항목이
> **"권한없음"**(개인 개발자는 "비즈니스 앱 전환"을 해야 요청 가능 — 사업자 없이도 개인
> 자격으로 전환 가능한지는 카카오 정책이라 확인 안 됨) 상태라 그대로 쓰면
> `"Invalid scope: account_email"`로 거부된다. 네이버와 동일한 방식(커스텀 Edge Function이
> Authorization Code 흐름을 직접 완결)으로 우회해 구현했다 — 코드는 이미 완성돼 있고,
> 아래 콘솔 설정만 하면 된다.
>
> 코드: `lib/kakaoAuth.ts`, `app/login/kakao-callback/page.tsx`,
> `supabase/functions/kakao-login/index.ts`. 정체성 정책은 네이버와 동일(합성 이메일
> `kakao-<카카오id>@kakao.socialauth.invalid`, DEC-004 참고).

**설정 순서**

1. **developers.kakao.com** 가입 → "내 애플리케이션" → 앱 생성
   - "회사명"은 사업자 없어도 본인 이름/프로젝트 이름 아무거나 입력 가능(실제 사업자 검증 안 함)
   - "앱 대표 도메인"은 `localhost` 등 로컬 주소를 거부하므로 **비워두고 넘어가면 된다**(선택 항목)
2. **제품 설정 → 카카오 로그인 → 일반** → "사용 설정" **ON**
3. **동의항목**에서 **"닉네임"만 필수 동의**로 설정(동의 목적 예: "회원가입 시 표시 이름으로
   사용하기 위해 수집합니다"). **"카카오계정(이메일)"은 "권한없음"이라 설정 자체가 안 되니
   그냥 건너뛴다** — 우리 구현은 이메일을 요청하지 않아서 문제없다.
4. **앱 설정 → 플랫폼 키** → `Default Rest API Key` 카드 오른쪽 **⋮ → 수정** 클릭
   - **"카카오 로그인 리다이렉트 URI"**에 등록:
     ```
     http://localhost:3000/login/kakao-callback
     ```
     (배포 후엔 실제 도메인의 같은 경로도 추가)
   - **REST API 키** 값을 복사해둔다(= Client ID)
5. 같은 "플랫폼 키" 페이지에서 **"클라이언트 시크릿"** 클릭 → **"카카오 로그인"** 줄(⚠
   "비즈니스 인증" 줄 아님, 바로 아래 있어서 헷갈리기 쉬움)의 **코드**를 복사, **활성화 ON**
   확인(= Client Secret)
6. Edge Function 배포 (네이버와 같은 방식)
   ```bash
   supabase functions deploy kakao-login
   supabase secrets set KAKAO_CLIENT_ID=복사한_REST_API_키 KAKAO_CLIENT_SECRET=복사한_시크릿_코드
   ```
   - **반드시 카카오 콘솔에서 직접 복사-붙여넣기**로 진행할 것 — `I`(대문자 아이)와
     `l`(소문자 엘)이 거의 구분 안 되는 폰트라 손으로 옮겨적으면 `invalid_client`(KOE010)로
     실패하기 쉽다(실제로 겪은 문제).
7. 앱의 `.env.local`
   ```
   NEXT_PUBLIC_KAKAO_CLIENT_ID=복사한_REST_API_키
   ```
8. 배포 환경에도 같은 `NEXT_PUBLIC_KAKAO_CLIENT_ID` 등록 + 카카오 콘솔 Redirect URI에
   실제 배포 도메인 추가

name: Deletion authorization

# Required status check: blocks merging a PR that deletes a VT Radar row
# (an ID missing from every data sheet in data/json/, not moved to
# Deprecated) unless an admin (.github/RADAR-ADMINS) has approved the PR.
#
# Runs on both PR content changes and new reviews -- a review submitted
# after this check already failed needs to re-run the check for the same
# commit, which only happens if pull_request_review also triggers it.
#
# Deliberately checks *approval*, not *merge*: this check runs before the
# Merge button is even clickable, so there's no way to know who will merge
# ahead of time -- only who has already reviewed. A repo admin can still
# merge past a failing check via branch protection's admin-bypass setting,
# the same way they can already bypass the required-review rule.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - "data/json/**"
  pull_request_review:
    types: [submitted]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: head

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: base

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Check for unauthorized deletions
        working-directory: head
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          python src/scripts/check_deletion_authorization.py \
            --base-dir ../base/data/json \
            --head-dir data/json \
            --admins-file .github/RADAR-ADMINS \
            --repo ${{ github.repository }} \
            --pr-number ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

- run: pip install -r src/scripts/requirements.txt

      - name: Sync xlsx to JSON
        env:
          PR_ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
        run: python src/scripts/xlsx_to_json.py --actor "@$PR_ACTOR"

      - name: Commit and push data/json/ if it changed
        run: |

"""Required status check: a PR that deletes a VT Radar row needs an admin's
approval before it can merge.

Compares data/json/*.json between a PR's base and head to find any row ID
that disappears from *every* data sheet (a true deletion, not a move to
another sheet -- xlsx_to_json.py already reports the same distinction on
stdout during conversion; this recomputes it independently since it runs
against the JSON diff in a PR, not against an xlsx being converted).

If no true deletion is found, the check passes immediately -- ordinary edits
never need an admin's attention. If one is found, the check only passes if
the PR already carries an APPROVED review from someone on the admin list
(.github/RADAR-ADMINS). This deliberately checks *approval*, not *merge*:
a required status check runs before the Merge button is even clickable, so
it has no way to know who will eventually click it -- only who has already
reviewed. (An earlier version of this design tried to key off who merges,
which turned out not to be checkable pre-merge at all.)

A repo admin can always merge past a failing required check via branch
protection's "include administrators" bypass -- this check doesn't need to
special-case a solo admin proposing their own deletion, the same way the
existing required-review rule doesn't either.

Usage:
    python check_deletion_authorization.py --base-dir DIR --head-dir DIR

Clients are web, Tauri (Windows/macOS), and iOS. Every client keeps a full local replica and works fully disconnected.

- **`EnumSchemaAlignmentTest`** reads the allowed values out of `pg_constraint` and compares them to the enum, then writes every value to the real table. The enum and the CHECK constraint are two declarations of one fact in different languages; nothing but this keeps them honest. The tree structure — folders, documents, trash. This is the Scrivener "binder."

|---|---|---|

| title | text | |

| content | jsonb | ProseMirror doc JSON |

| notes | text, nullable | document notes (rich text or plain) |
| version | bigint | incremented per content save |

Manual or auto point-in-time captures of a document's content (Scrivener's snapshot feature).

escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing

escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative

Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

data; nothing may answer 500; and the victim's project must be unchanged
afterwards. Reading the mapping rather than a hand-written list means a new
controller method that forgets its authorization check fails immediately.

fix(gateway): make show_* actually work in a mapped room (#17)

* fix(gateway): carry the adapter's visual/file capability into node turns

The runtime MCP is default-deny for `show_html`, `show_mermaid`,
`show_image`, `show_video`, `publish_html` and the file-delivery tools:
`buildNegotiumMcpServer` registers them only when the context says
`visualTools`/`fileDeliveryTools` are true, because only an adapter with
a visual panel and a chat file surface knows whether that output would be
rendered or silently dropped.

`submitRuntimeGatewayTurn` had no way to say so. It builds the durable
turn request the worker later runs, and the worker builds the runtime MCP
from that request's `execution`, so every turn arriving over the gateway
got the tools stripped — while the prompt built for the same turn still
advertised them. A mapped room's agent was told to call `show_html` and
then handed an MCP that did not have it.

Add the capability to the contract and thread it through to `execution`.
It stays out of the idempotency payload hash: it describes the caller,
not the message, so hashing it would only turn an adapter upgrade into a
409 for keys already in flight.

`show_png` is fixed in the same pass. It is a pure alias of `show_image`
kept for Otium prompts and sessions persisted before the rename; Otium's
own hub both registers and intercepts it, but the node did neither, so a
mapped room resuming such a session would call a tool that is not there.
It rides the same gate as the tools it aliases.

* feat(gateway): let a host read back visuals and files a node produced

The capability work made `show_html` callable in a mapped room. It did
not make it *visible*: the turn runs on the node, so the visual is
rendered into the node's own store and the runtime event carries a URL
under a topic id only the node knows. A hub that owns the room but not
the execution has nothing to serve its panel from, and its visual route
looks the id up in its own database and 404s. Media and delivered files
are worse — the contract could upload *to* a node and never read back, so
the bytes had no path home at all.

Add the two reads that were missing:

- `GET /topics/<id>/visuals/<vizId>` returns the visual in a portable
  shape (kind, title, rendered html, the agent's own source, and the
  media file id) so a host can re-insert it into its own store.
- `GET /files/<fileId>` returns bytes from the node file store, which
  covers both the media behind a visual and a delivered chat file.

Copying rather than proxying is deliberate: the host keeps serving a
visual after the node goes offline, its own access control stays in
charge of who can see the room, and a panel load does not become a
second network hop that can fail. `fileId` is scoped to the node that
produced it, so a copying host re-uploads under an id of its own.

Both are additive reads on the v1 contract. Nothing grants the tools yet
— that stays default-deny until the hub side of the copy exists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(runtime): let adapter-less turns inherit the room's granted tools

A capability describes the surface a room is rendered on, not the message
that triggered a turn. Whether `show_html` output can be displayed
depends on whether Otium is drawing the panel, and that is equally true
for a user's message, a `tell`, a cron job, and an auto-continue resume.

Only a user turn arrives from an adapter, though, so only a user turn
carried the grant. `triggerTopicAiTurn` — session-comm tell/ask,
config-change auto-continue, cron, subagent reports — calls `startAiTurn`
with no capabilities at all, so all of those ran without the tools. A
scheduled job in an Otium room could not draw a chart into the panel
sitting in front of the user, and a turn resumed after a model switch
lost `show_html` mid-conversation.

Record the grant on the room when a turn does carry it, and inherit it
when a turn does not. Absence defers; an explicit `false` still means no,
so Terminal and Telegram, which state their capabilities outright, are
unchanged.

Deliberately recorded rather than derived from `topic.surface`, even
though the three adapters map onto it exactly. Deriving would grant the
tools to any host serving an `otium` room — including one too old to
carry a node's rendered visual back to its panel — which reintroduces the
callable-tool-with-no-output failure precisely during a rollout. A
recorded grant only ever says what an adapter actually asked for.

Re-recorded per turn rather than once at room creation, so a host that
gains or loses a surface takes effect from its next turn. Dropped with
the room in `deleteTopicCascade`.

Review found the new `GET /files/<fileId>` read bypassed workspace

The visual read was scope-checked, but the file read had no topic to
check against and delegated authorization to the node file store on
`(fileId, user)` alone. Every mapped room executes as the same `local`
principal and Otium always sends `user=local`, so that ACL is satisfied
by construction for any caller: a gateway scoped to workspace A that
learned a workspace-B file UUID would be handed B's bytes, even though
every one of B's rooms 404s for it. UUID entropy made that hard to reach
by accident, which is not the same as enforcing M-8.

Address the read through its room instead. The route is now
`GET /topics/<id>/files/<fileId>`, behind the same `topicInRequestScope`
check as every other topic-scoped route, and the file must actually
belong to the room named in the path.

The test asserts both halves: the owning room serves the bytes, and the
same UUID named through a sibling room does not.

fix(idor-scanner): match ORM method names by prefix, not exact string

isDataAccess() compared each call name against a fixed list of exact
strings (findone, findbyid...). A real ORM method absent from that
list (TypeORM's findOneBy, Mongoose's findByIdAndUpdate, etc.) was
silently skipped by the scanner. If the same method also contained a
recognized, filtered call, the deterministic guard could still emit a
"safe" verdict at zero LLM cost while the unrecognized, unfiltered
call was never examined — the same class of silent false negative
fixed last night, this time on the method name instead of the scope
window.

Every existing fixture name is already a prefix of itself, so no
behavior changes for recognized names; an unrecognized prefix match
can only push a route into the LLM-reviewed grey zone, never produce
a false "safe" verdict.

   an athlete could do neither to anything a coach sent them, even though
   every "Send a copy" is already a fully independent programs row (see

   set_active_program's explicit permission check to accept the assigned
   athlete as well as the owner, and adds an additive RLS policy letting an
   athlete delete their own assigned row. Since each assignment is its own
   copy, an athlete deleting or reactivating theirs can never touch the

explanation:
Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level

fix(red-team): address 8 security vulnerabilities from Red Team audit

1. ATTACK-01: Fake promo codes → database-backed validation with PromoCode model + migration 021
2. ATTACK-04: XSS in email → html.escape() + URL scheme validation on all user-controlled fields
3. ATTACK-05: CSRF bypass → extended CSRF protection to all mutating endpoints (with webhook/auth exempts)
4. ATTACK-06: Entitlement race condition → atomic UPDATE with WHERE clause (consumed+qty <= quantity)
5. ATTACK-09: IDOR in prompt compiler → pass user_id to compile_prompt, verify project ownership
6. ATTACK-15: Mock payment mode → startup guard raises if YOOKASSA creds missing in production
7. ATTACK-16: Audit log silent bypass → changed logger.debug to logger.warning
8. ATTACK-19: Missing security headers → added SecurityHeadersMiddleware (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
9. ATTACK-20: Contact import validation → added input validation, length limits, date parsing, contacts limit

fix(security): AuthPrincipal.userId ở certificates/grading + chặn quyền rỗng

Lỗi có sẵn từ P5, phát hiện khi verify P7 (KHÔNG do P7 gây ra).

Gốc: `@CurrentUser()` trả `AuthPrincipal { userId }`, nhưng certificates.service.ts và
grading.service.ts khai kiểu `AuthUser` rồi đọc `currentUser.id` / `currentUser.roles`
→ luôn undefined lúc chạy. Hậu quả đã xác nhận trên DB dev:

- `getEffectivePermissions(undefined)` → `userRole.findMany({ where: { userId: undefined } })`
  — Prisma coi undefined là "không lọc" → trả MỌI user_role → hợp nhất quyền của mọi role
  ≈ super_admin. Mọi kiểm quyền trong certificates đều pass.
- `listMine` lọc `userId: undefined` → trả chứng chỉ của MỌI học viên.
- `POST /certificates/:id/revoke` và `GET /certificates/:id/pdf` (chỉ JwtAuthGuard, scope
  kiểm trong service) → user bất kỳ thu hồi / tải được chứng chỉ người khác.
- `GET /classes/:classId/my-gradebook` ném 500 PrismaClientValidationError.

Sửa:
- certificates + grading nhận `AuthPrincipal` và dùng `currentUser.userId`. Bỏ shortcut
  `currentUser.roles?.includes('admin')` — admin/super_admin nhận quyền ở phạm vi GLOBAL
  nên `hasPermission` đã phủ (đối chiếu seed: cả hai có certificate.*/grade.read).
- `RbacService.getEffectivePermissions` trả quyền RỖNG khi userId falsy, không chạm DB —
  phòng thủ chiều sâu để một chỗ gọi sai không bao giờ thành cấp quyền toàn hệ thống.
- Test hồi quy (+6): rbac userId rỗng (undefined/null/''), revoke 403 + tra đúng userId,
  listMine lọc đúng userId, getPdfBuffer IDOR 403.

Verify: `pnpm validate` 16/16, api 180 test. Live sau vá: my-gradebook 200; HV không sở hữu
`/certificates/mine` = 0 (chủ sở hữu = 1), `:id/pdf` 403, `:id/revoke` 403; GV vẫn đọc được
`/certificates/class/:id` và `/gradebook` (200).

Ghi nhận nợ MỚI (chưa vá, có từ P6/D1): sinh PDF chứng chỉ 500 với tiếng Việt —
`WinAnsi cannot encode "ơ"` do pdf-lib StandardFonts; cần nhúng font Unicode qua fontkit.

fix(api): close the agent-token gaps found by the codex gate

Critical: the MCP-only rule was scoped to the /api/v1 prefix, so POST /logout —
the one root-level auth:sanctum route — still accepted agent bearers, giving an
agent a human-only action and a token-validity oracle. The refusal now sits on
both route groups; accepting a token is a positive capability exactly one
surface will opt into (#135). The IDOR sweep enumerates every registered route
instead of a prefix, and proves its two exemptions authenticate nothing.

High: Sanctum's provider hoists EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful to the front
of the middleware priority list at boot, which sorted the session/CSRF stack
ahead of the refusal — a bearer with a first-party Origin opened a database
session and hit 419 before being refused. AppServiceProvider now hoists the
refusal after Sanctum's provider; asserted on pipeline order and as zero
queries on a rejected request. Mint and its audit record are one transaction;
revoke records through recordSafely and only the request that removed the row
records an event; the Policy trait fails closed on any persistent token that is
not an AgentToken.

Also: no-store on the mint response, a dismiss action for the revealed value,
error-vs-empty on the settings list, deny-as-not-found for a foreign token id,
and a per-member token cap that bounds the unpaginated list.

Dismissals and deferrals recorded in TODOS.md.

fix(api): close the agent-token gaps found by the codex gate

Critical: the MCP-only rule was scoped to the /api/v1 prefix, so POST /logout —
the one root-level auth:sanctum route — still accepted agent bearers, giving an
agent a human-only action and a token-validity oracle. The refusal now sits on
both route groups; accepting a token is a positive capability exactly one
surface will opt into (#135). The IDOR sweep enumerates every registered route
instead of a prefix, and proves its two exemptions authenticate nothing.

High: Sanctum's provider hoists EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful to the front
of the middleware priority list at boot, which sorted the session/CSRF stack
ahead of the refusal — a bearer with a first-party Origin opened a database
session and hit 419 before being refused. AppServiceProvider now hoists the
refusal after Sanctum's provider; asserted on pipeline order and as zero
queries on a rejected request. Mint and its audit record are one transaction;
revoke records through recordSafely and only the request that removed the row
records an event; the Policy trait fails closed on any persistent token that is
not an AgentToken.

Also: no-store on the mint response, a dismiss action for the revealed value,
error-vs-empty on the settings list, deny-as-not-found for a foreign token id,
and a per-member token cap that bounds the unpaginated list.

  the stub. Never dangling-referenced, never fabricated, never omitted.

  resolved) AND unconditionally derives what the ref-form ids WOULD have
  been from the SAME row data, emitting a ProjectionTombstone for both the

Fix user privilege escalation bug (#13976)

The AddUser() API endpoint was accepting a policy field. 
This API is used to update a user's secret key and account 
status, and allows a regular user to update their own secret key. 

The policy update is also applied though does not appear to 
be used by any existing client-side functionality.

This fix changes the accepted request body type and removes 
the ability to apply policy changes as that is possible via the 
policy set API.

NOTE: Changing passwords can be disabled as a workaround
for this issue by adding an explicit "Deny" rule to disable the API
for users.

explanation:
Fix wrong-verdict, safety and trace bugs found in a full code review

Nine defects, several of which could make this tool report a green verdict on
a real bug. Verified against live SFMC plus a local CSV file (23 checks).

Wrong verdicts:

- Compare.evaluate fell back to lexicographic comparison whenever either side
  was not numeric, and String.valueOf(null) is "null". A NULL column therefore
  satisfied ">= 100", because "null" sorts after "100". Null now fails every
  ordering comparator and participates only in eq/ne.
- The same function coerced both sides through BigDecimal, so "007" equalled
  "7" and "01234" equalled "1234" — silently passing assertions on zero-padded
  ids, zip codes and order numbers. Numeric comparison now requires an actual
  number on one side; two strings compare exactly. assert_query reports which
  rule decided the verdict, so a recorded check can be audited.
- Timestamps were formatted with no fractional-seconds field, so .123456789
  serialized as plain seconds. Millisecond-precision values compared equal to
  each other and to whole seconds, making that class of ticket untestable.
  Seconds are still always present (the PR #1 fix); fractions are appended only
  when non-zero.
- Types.FLOAT read through getFloat(). JDBC maps FLOAT to double — only REAL is
  single-precision — so every SQL FLOAT column was rounded to ~7 digits before
  any assertion saw it (1234567.891234567 -> 1234567.875).

Safety:

- read_only was enforced by only two of the eight tools that execute SQL. Two
  paths wrote freely: execute_query routes EXEC through Statement.execute(),
  and execute_java hands snippet code a live Connection. The guard now lives in
  the JDBC proxy layer, the only placement that can cover snippet code, and
  refuses anything not plainly a read with SQLState 25006. EXEC/CALL count as
  writes, since a procedure body is opaque. Documented as a guard, not a
  sandbox: getMetaData().getConnection() and unwrap() still escape it.
- The capture addon logged Authorization/Cookie verbatim, leaving live bearer
  tokens in the system temp directory (73 across two logs on this machine).
  They are now replaced by length + truncated SHA-256, which still identifies
  a token or a refresh. Bodies are capped (JDBC_MCP_MITM_MAX_BODY, 64 KB):
  uncapped bodies are what grew a single entry to 435 KB.
- export_results silently truncated whatever was at file_path; it now refuses
  without overwrite=true, and streams rows instead of materializing the whole
  result set, which was the documented path for "full exports".
- set_jvm_proxy set process-global proxy properties permanently, rerouting
  every later connection in the server. Now reference-counted and restored on
  disconnect or idle eviction.

Missing traces:

- executeBatch/addBatch were never intercepted, so the batch checklist ran with
  an empty intercepted_calls. Batch calls now report batch_size and summed row
  counts, with the first parameter set for prepared batches.
- prepareCall returned an unwrapped CallableStatement: no trace, and no
  ProxyResultSet, so the query deadline from PR #12 did not cover procedures.
- Failures returned a bare {"error": …} with no trace — precisely the calls
  being investigated, while the pass criteria are written in terms of
  intercepted_calls[*].error. compare_queries never returned traces at all and
  its second beginCall() wiped the first query's log.
- execute_java swapped the global System.out and restored it in a finally. A
  snippet outliving its timeout is only interrupted, so its next println landed
  on the real stdout — the JSON-RPC channel — and could break the session.
  Capture is now bound to the thread, not to a time window, and capped.

Also: get_metadata called getColumns once per table (an N+1 the checklists warn
about) and returned an uncapped bare array that could exhaust the caller's
context; it now makes one call, caps results, and reports counts. setNull was
traced as the type code 12 rather than null. Text truncation compared char
length against a byte budget. The connect probe's request appears in the capture
with no matching intercepted_call, so probe_sql is now reported.

Removed get_usage_stats: all five of its fields are already in the "Session
activity" section of get_test_report, and estimated tokens are on every
response's _meta.

def _decode_identity_bytes(raw: Any) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Decode an FC43 object defensively. Returns (text, decoded_cleanly).

    UTF-8 is tried FIRST, not ASCII. A Chinese, Japanese or German vendor name is
    ordinary in this market — 汇川, 三菱, Müller — and an ASCII-first decoder marks
    every one of them "not clean", which puts a corruption warning on a perfectly
    good asset register row and teaches the reader to ignore the flag. Only bytes
    that are genuinely not UTF-8 fall back to latin-1, and only those are flagged:
    latin-1 never raises, so it can silently mis-render, and the operator should
    know which fields might be wrong.

An authenticated member of one project can modify and delete members of
another project, without knowledge of this other project's private
code. This can be further exploited to access all bills of another project
without knowledge of this other project's private code.

With the default configuration, anybody is allowed to create a new
project. An attacker can create a new project and then use it to become
authenticated and exploit this flaw. As such, the exposure is similar to
an unauthenticated attack, because it is trivial to become authenticated.

This issue was caused by a wrong database queries in PersonQuery.

fix(console): the checkout spec sends the Idempotency-Key its client always sends (AGL-2163)

A stale fixture, NOT a money-path defect — checked first, because the red
looked like one. The Billing page mints a key per attempt and sends
`Idempotency-Key` on every `/api/billing/checkout` call
(`app/(app)/[orgSlug]/billing/page.tsx`), and the route consumes it into
`claimAttempt`. Both halves are correct and it is the only caller. The
console checkout is protected.

What was wrong is that this spec could not have told the difference. Its
hand-written `pluginRequestFromWeb` forwarded three headers BY NAME —
`authorization`, `origin`, `host` — so the route's
`headers['idempotency-key']` was always empty no matter what the fixture
sent. Another closed-world mock, this one blinding a money-path suite to
the exact property AGL-2163 is about. When AGL-2163 made the keyless
branch `console.warn` that it is an unprotected money call, this spec's
blanket `expect(warnings).toHaveLength(0)` — there to catch a MISSING
metered item — caught its own unfaithful request instead.

So: the real `pluginRequestFromWeb` via `requireActual` (it is pure — no
Next internals), with `origin`/`host` layered UNDER the real headers
because the platform adds them and a bare Web `Request` cannot; a request
that carries the key; and an `apiIdempotency` store double that models
the one Firestore behaviour the claim is built on — `create()` REJECTS on
an existing document, which is the whole dedupe primitive. A double that
resolved instead would fabricate a green for a route that double-charges.
One key per call, because one call here is one attempt: a shared key
would make the second call a REPLAY, which never reaches Stripe, leaving
every assertion checking a stale `capturedBody`.

Forced red, twice. Dropping the `Idempotency-Key` header: 3 failed, the
UNPROTECTED-money-call warning back on every attempt. Pointing
`STRIPE_PRICE_METERED_YEARLY` at the monthly id: 2 failed, including
"NEVER puts the monthly metered price on an annual subscription" — the
mixed-interval assertion Stripe rejects outright. The guard still bites.

Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

fix(api): close the agent-token gaps found by the codex gate

Critical: the MCP-only rule was scoped to the /api/v1 prefix, so POST /logout —
the one root-level auth:sanctum route — still accepted agent bearers, giving an
agent a human-only action and a token-validity oracle. The refusal now sits on
both route groups; accepting a token is a positive capability exactly one
surface will opt into (#135). The IDOR sweep enumerates every registered route
instead of a prefix, and proves its two exemptions authenticate nothing.

High: Sanctum's provider hoists EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful to the front
of the middleware priority list at boot, which sorted the session/CSRF stack
ahead of the refusal — a bearer with a first-party Origin opened a database
session and hit 419 before being refused. AppServiceProvider now hoists the
refusal after Sanctum's provider; asserted on pipeline order and as zero
queries on a rejected request. Mint and its audit record are one transaction;
revoke records through recordSafely and only the request that removed the row
records an event; the Policy trait fails closed on any persistent token that is
not an AgentToken.

Also: no-store on the mint response, a dismiss action for the revealed value,
error-vs-empty on the settings list, deny-as-not-found for a foreign token id,
and a per-member token cap that bounds the unpaginated list.

Dismissals and deferrals recorded in TODOS.md.

fix(backend): return 400/404 for bad input instead of 500 (#14)

Missing required query params, malformed JSON, invalid enum values in
request bodies, and unknown-resource lookups all bubbled up as 500
Internal Server Error via the fallback exception handler.

Add typed handlers to `GlobalExceptionHandler`:
- `MissingServletRequestParameterException` → 400 with the missing
  param name in `fieldErrors`.
- `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` → 400 with the field and the
  rejected value (e.g. `/metrics/date/not-a-date`).
- `HttpMessageNotReadableException` → 400. When the cause is a Jackson
  `InvalidFormatException` on an enum target, list the allowed values
  in the field-error message so clients see e.g.
  "Not a valid WeightGoal value. Allowed: [LOSE_SLOW, LOSE_MODERATE,
  LOSE_FAST, MAINTAIN, GAIN_SLOW, GAIN_MODERATE]".
- `NoResourceFoundException` → 404 with a generic message.

Also:
- Refresh `docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md`: Phase 3 (Nutrition) is complete —
  service, controller, and Angular UI all exist and work end-to-end.
- Rewrite `README.md § Authentication`: the refresh token is set as an
  HttpOnly cookie by `/auth/login` and `/auth/register` and read from
  that cookie by `/auth/refresh` — not from the `Authorization` header.
  Document the required `startDate`/`endDate` on `/workouts/history`
  and the body-required `date` on `POST /workouts`.

Unit-tested via `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest` (60/60 pass) and
end-to-end verified against a jar built from this branch.

1.9.3 - `unreleased`
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Fixed arbitrary certificate revocation at the CA (`GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67`_). Certificate identity was tracked
  only by Lemur's internal database row, not by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated authUser could
  upload a duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing ``authority_id`` and
  ``serial``) and then revoke it via ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``, causing the CA to revoke the
  real certificate belonging to another authUser. ``POST /api/1/certificates/upload`` now requires
  ``AuthorityPermission`` on the specified authority, and rejects uploads whose ``(authority_id, serial)``
  pair already matches an existing certificate with a ``409`` response. ``PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke``
  now also checks authorization and endpoint attachment against every certificate row sharing
  ``(authority_id, serial)`` with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request, closing the
  gap for any duplicate rows that already exist.

fix: close the anchor-guard composition gaps (by Wren)

Round-8 review blockers from Lumen on #514. All four were composition
failures: each guard was individually correct and defeated by what ran
after it.

1. A supplied canonical UUID was being invalidated by slug ambiguity.
   Discovery exists to gate the SLUG fallback, not to veto an identity we
   already hold — with a UUID in hand every tier below is UUID-scoped and a
   duplicate slug cannot reach them. Ambiguity now refuses only when there
   is no canonical id.

2. Both anchor helpers could accept a row carrying sb_id=OTHER through the
   absent+slug fallback. A row that CARRIES an identity must match it
   canonically, always; only a null-sb row may use the slug, and only on a
   positive `absent`.

3. The findByUserAndAgent UUID option was never passed and was missing from
   ISessionRepository, so canonical A still reused sibling B. Both fixed.
   Ambiguous unthreaded work now skips general reuse entirely rather than
   falling back to the slug — it is not refused, since unthreaded work does
   not lease a studio, but it must not be silently attached to another
   identity's session either.

4. A failed explicit-studio authorization returned an ordinary `refused`
   tier, which is only inspected at the create boundary — while alias,
   threadKey, default-session and general reuse all run BEFORE it. A
   matching fallback therefore satisfied a request whose explicit anchor had
   just been rejected. Invalid explicit anchors are now fatal at the point of
   rejection, as is the ambiguity refusal, which the reuse rungs could
   otherwise slug-match past.

Tests: the guard regressions are rewritten to the pattern review asked for —
guard PLUS a plausible later fallback, rather than a guard with every later
rung mocked absent. Each now seeds alias/threadKey/general reuse with a
session the ladder would happily return, so the test fails if the guard
leaks instead of merely proving nothing was available.

150 session-service (was 145) + 8 routing-hold + 8 sender-context; full API
2409; typecheck at the known five-error baseline.

Mutation-checked: making the explicit-anchor refusal non-fatal, admitting an
sb_id-bearing row through the slug fallback, or letting ambiguity veto a
supplied UUID each turn exactly one test red.

The positive-case test is worth noting: its first version asserted only "does
not throw" and failed against the ORDINARY no-route refusal, which is correct
behaviour. It now supplies a UUID-scoped route-pattern studio and asserts the
session is created against it, so success distinguishes "reached the
UUID-scoped tiers" from "was not refused for some other reason".

Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:

None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.
